We present a straightforward calibration method for the small variation in the corresponding coefficient from channel-to-channel.</summary><hostname>arXiv</hostname><publisher>JINST</publisher><author_list><author name="Sebastian White" affiliation="Laboratory of Instrumentation and Experimental Particle Physics (LIP), Portugal" /><author name="Alessio Boletti" affiliation="Laboratory of Instrumentation and Experimental Particle Physics (LIP), Portugal" /></author_list><url>https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.07127v4</url><arxiv_url>https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.07127v4</arxiv_url><arxiv_id>2507.07127v4</arxiv_id></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:33"><title>Development and Application Study of the High-rate Multi-gap Resistive Plate Chamber for CBM Experiment</title><summary>多气隙电阻板室（mrpc）是具有平行电极结构的新型气体探测器。因其优秀的性能和相对便宜的造价，经过将近二十年的发展，如今mrpc已经在高能物理和核物理实验中得到了广泛而成功的应用。未来在德国反质子和离子研究设施（fair）建成的压缩重子物质实验（cbm）中，将采用mrpc组成120 m²的飞行时间测量系统（TOF）。模拟结果证明，CBM-TOF系统需要承受高达30 kHz/cm²的粒子通量，同时达到80 ps的时间分辨能力和超过95%的探测效率。清华大学将为CBM合作组研制具有高计数率能力和高时间分辨率的MRPC探测器，这将是高计数率MRPC探测器在物理实验中的第一次大规模实际应用。随着包括CBM在内的物理实验加速器亮度不断提升的趋势，MRPC的工作气体污染不可再被忽视。其本质原因是气体在高粒子通量下消耗更快导致供给不足，失去吸收电子和抑制流光的能力，产物还会对探测器结构产生损害。气体污染现象曾在STAR实验中观测到，在计数率更高的CBM实验中其影响将更为显著。论文致力于CBM实验高计数率MRPC的研制与应用研究。结合低电阻玻璃技术设计了真实尺寸MRPC的结构和参数，并在多次束流实验中验证了它具有稳定的97%探测效率和60 ps的时间分辨率，成为首个被合作组确定为最终方案的候选MRPC。针对FAIR第0阶段运行计划的需求，圆满完成首批76个探测器的小批量生产，其中48个安装于STAR实验的东部端盖作为eTOF系统为BES-II运行提供重要的物理信息。论文对2018年STAR实验运行中的27 GeV Au+Au对撞数据进行离线刻度分析，结果证明高计数率MRPC时间分辨可达60 ps，同时首次实现了STAR端盖区域的粒子鉴别，对(π+K)/p的鉴别能力可达3.0 GeV/c。高计数率MRPC在物理实验中的首次成功应用为在CBM和STAR上获得重要物理成果提供了有力保障。论文同时系统研究了CBM实验高计数率引起的MRPC气体污染现象。分别通过数值模拟和X射线实验研究影响污染的各项因素，最终得出采用极小流气体积可大大降低探测器内部污染浓度的结论。由此提出可应用于CBM实验的自流气MRPC解决方案，该设计对包括CBM在内的高亮度物理实验探测谱仪中的气体探测器设计具有重要意义。</summary><hostname>GSI Indico</hostname><publisher>Degree Thesis</publish

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="AI 时钟抖动补偿 神经网络 机器学习 TDC 时幅转换" search_time="2026年5月19日11时37分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:36"><title>一种基于BiCNN的ToF测距精度补偿方法</title><summary>基于飞行时间法(ToF)的脉冲激光测距技术,凭借其脉冲宽度窄、峰值功率大等特性,已在非合作目标探测领域获得广泛应用。然而,现有基于阈值判别的测距系统仍存在以下技术瓶颈:1)回波光功率波动引起回波信号前后沿产生游走误差;2)波形抖动和时钟漂移引发测量数据异常波动或信号丢失;3)系统时延导致固定测量误差。针对以上问题,提出了一种基于双向卷积神经网络的ToF测距精度补偿方法,该方法首先通过双向长短期记忆网络的多层约束来信息实现脉宽异常检测,继而采用一维卷积神经网络进行回归分析以实现自适应精度补偿。在4~110m量程范围内重复测距实验中,系统测距偏差稳定在0.05~0.33m区间,相较传统多项式拟合方法,测量精度提升率达72.5%,有效验证了所提方法的工程实用性。</summary><hostname>Researching</hostname><publisher>SEMICONDUCTOR OPTOELECTRONICS</publisher><author_list><author name="亓林" affiliation="重庆光电技术研究所" /><author name="高传顺" affiliation="重庆光电技术研究所" /><author name="林珑君" affiliation="重庆光电技术研究所" /><author name="伍明娟" affiliation="重庆光电技术研究所" /><author name="曹飞" affiliation="重庆光电技术研究所" /><author name="朱斌" affiliation="重庆光电技术研究所" /><author name="吴海游" affiliation="重庆光电技术研究所" /></author_list><url>https://www.researching.cn/ArticlePdf/m00031/2025/46/1/3.pdf</url><publish_time>2025年2月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:37"><title>Label-free timing analysis of modularized nuclear detectors with physics-constrained deep learning</title><summary>Pulse timing is an important topic in nuclear instrumentation, with far-reaching applications from high energy physics to radiation imaging. While high-speed analog-to-digital converters become more and more developed and accessible, their potential uses and merits in nuclear detector signal processing are still uncertain, partially due to associated timing algorithms which are not fully understood and utilized. In this paper, we propose a novel method based on deep learning for timing analysis of modularized nuclear detectors without explicit needs of labelling event data. By taking advantage of the inner time correlation of individual detectors, a label-free loss function with a specially designed regularizer is formed to supervise the training of neural networks towards a meaningful and accurate mapping function. We mathematically demonstrate the existence of the optimal function desired by the method, and give a systematic algorithm for training and calibration of the model. The proposed method is validated on two experimental datasets. In the toy experiment, the neural network model achieves the single-channel time resolution of 8.8 ps and exhibits robustness against concept drift in the dataset. In the electromagnetic calorimeter experiment, several neural network models (FC, CNN and LSTM) are tested to show their conformance to the underlying physical constraint and to judge their performance against traditional methods. In total, the proposed method works well in either ideal or noisy experimental condition and recovers the time information from waveform samples successfully and precisely.</summary><hostname>arXiv</hostname><author_list><author name="Pengcheng Ai" affiliation="1 PLAC, Key Laboratory of Quark and Lepton Physics (MOE), Central China Normal University, Wuhan, 430079, China; 2 Hubei Provincial Engineering Research Center of Silicon Pixel Chip & Detection Technology, Wuhan, 430079, China" /><author name="Le Xiao" affiliation="1 PLAC, Key Laboratory of Quark and Lepton Physics (MOE), Central China Normal University, Wuhan, 430079, China; 2 Hubei Provincial Engineering Research Center of Silicon Pixel Chip & Detection Technology, Wuhan, 430079, China" /><author name="Zhi Deng" affiliation="3 Key Laboratory of Particle and Radiation Imaging (MOE), Department of Engineering Physics, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China" /><author name="Yi Wang" affiliation="3 Key Laboratory of Particle and Radiation Imaging (MOE), Department of Engineering Physics, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China" /><author name="Xiangming Sun" affiliation="1 PLAC, Key Laboratory of Quark and Lepton Physics (MOE), Central China Normal University, Wuhan, 430079, China; 2 Hubei Provincial Engineering Research Center of Silicon Pixel Chip & Detection Technology, Wuhan, 430079, China" /><author name="Guangming Huang" affilia

从系统架构看，模块化分层架构（“大脑-小脑”）将高层规划与推理与底层运动控制和稳定分离；端到端VLA将视觉、语言和动作在模型中进行端到端对齐与联合训练，追求从感知到行动的统一；基于感知-决策-行动的分层架构（如“大脑”负责高层任务规划和推理，“小脑”负责底层运动控制和稳定）是另一主流选择<cite id="14">“大脑”模型进行高层任务规划和推理，"小脑"模型负责底层的运动控制和稳定。</cite><cite id="14">端到端VLA：将视觉、语言和动作在模型中进行端到端对齐与联合训练，追求输入的感知信息到动作输出的端到端对齐，强调模型在真实世界中的任务完成能力。</cite><cite id="14">模块化分层架构(大脑-小脑)</cite>。具身智能系统还需整合感知、决策、行动，形成闭环控制，以实现与环境的持续交互<cite id="7">Embodied intelligence emphasizes that true intelligence arises from the dynamic interplay of brain, body, and environment, closing the perception-action loop.</cite>。

Large language models (LLMs), as well as models capable of generating images and videos, are already enjoying broad adoption. So far, users mostly interact with AI through textual interfaces, such as chatbots. Future AI systems are expected to have more advanced capabilities, functioning as “agents” that can search the web, buy or sell goods, engage in dialogue and make inquiries. They might be adapted for broader roles, such as virtual assistants, personal coaches, or artificial scientists. We can also expect fine-tuning through human feedback to better align our outputs with human imperatives and, potentially, human values. Future AI systems may operate as coordinated collectives: federated networks of AI agents working together toward shared goals. Even more transformative are robotic and embodied AI systems: robots that can perceive and act in the physical world—for example, at home, in factories or hospitals—alone or in collaboration with other AIs and humans. Future AI systems may operate as coordinated collectives: federated networks of AI agents working together toward shared goals. Many of these developments are already underway, and there is an expectation that these advanced AI models will transform our societies. Looking further ahead, we can imagine a future where such systems interact with humans in increasingly integrated ways, potentially augmenting human cognitive capabilities—such as perception, decision-making or memory—and situational awareness, based upon an understanding of the world. These systems may go beyond the traditional notion of “tools”, as they require a degree of autonomy, purposive epistemic and instrumental goals and continuously adapt from our interactions with them may evolve from simple tool to collaborative or even competitive relationships towards hybrid human-AI societies. Our focus here is on a potential paradigm shift: from the current approach of training AI models in a largely passive manner using massive datasets of human-generated content toward more interactive learning. This emerging approach more closely mirrors how biological agents learn through deliberative engagement with their physical and social environments. Such a shift raises profound scientific, technological and societal questions. What would it mean to build AI systems that learn not merely by observing but by acting, experimenting and adapting in real-time? What are the ethical and social implications of developing AI agents capable of modifying the world around them, much like biological organisms do? In this commentary, we examine the foundations, opportunities and challenges of this new direction in AI research. The challenge of scaling up generative AI to embodied settings The success of generative AI systems is driven by the development of large-scale predictive models trained on massive datasets. A prominent example is LLMs, which are trained to generate text by predicting the next word in a sequence. These models are often referred to as “foundation models” because their learned representations can be adapted for a wide range of downstream tasks. For instance, a foundation model can be fine-tuned to power chatbots that engage in human-like conversations, or to create domain-specific assistants capable of answering questions about topics such as medicine or sports. The same methodology has led to foundation models developed for image and video generation, or integrating multiple modalities, such as text and videos. # 全球数学与量子计算交叉领域主要研究团队及其成果综述

## 研究团队概览
数学与量子计算交叉领域汇聚了多个顶尖团队，涵盖量子算法、复杂性理论、量子信息基础、量子纠错与拓扑量子计算等方向。代表性团队包括：哈佛大学量子科学中心（Harvard Quantum Science Center，HQC）与量子科学与工程中心（Q-SE），麻省理工学院（MIT）量子工程与科学中心（CQEC），加州理工学院（Caltech）量子信息与计算小组，剑桥大学理论物理系，牛津大学量子信息组，苏黎世联邦理工学院（ETH Zurich）量子计算与信息中心，以及荷兰代尔夫特理工大学（Delft）的Delft Quantum Institute。这些团队在理论与应用层面均取得显著成果，部分成果已推动量子算法与硬件的协同演进<cite id="2">Harrow 与 Farhi 提出 QAOA 并论证其潜在量子霸权</cite><cite id="12">Wocian 与 Yard 关于琼斯多项式的量子算法及其在量子复杂性中的应用</cite><cite id="13">Bub 等人关于量子计算基础与量子模拟的理论研究</cite><cite id="26">Van Apeldoorn 等人在量子 SDP �求解器的进展</cite><cite id="34">Preskill 关于量子计算基础与错误修正的综述</cite><cite id="35">Freedman 等人关于拓扑量子计算的综述</cite><cite id="39">Nikolov 等人关于量子算法的综述</cite>。

## 核心研究方向与代表性成果
### 量子算法与复杂性理论
Harrow、Farhi 等人提出量子近似优化算法（QAOA），并论证其在特定问题上难以被经典采样模拟，为“量子霸权”提供了复杂性视角；同时，Harrow 等人的奠基性工作（如 HHL 线性系统求解器）确立了量子算法在大规模线性代数问题上的潜力<cite id="2">QAOA 与量子霸权论证</cite><cite id="22">HHL 算法概述</cite><cite id="23">HHL 算法的复杂度分析</cite>。此外，针对量子线性系统求解器的下界研究进一步明确了其复杂度边界，例如 sparsity 依赖项的刻画，为算法优化提供了理论支撑<cite id="1">QLS 下界中 sparsity 依赖项的建立</cite>。

### 量子信息基础与模拟
团队围绕量子计算基础（如测量、纠缠、非定域性）与量子模拟展开系统研究，例如 Bub 等人的工作探讨了量子测量与模拟的理论框架，为理解量子算法的物理实现提供了基础支撑<cite id="13">量子计算基础与量子模拟的理论研究</cite>。

### 量子纠错与容错
Preskill 的综述系统梳理了量子纠错与容错的理论框架，明确了实现可扩展量子计算的关键挑战与路径，为工程化设计提供了数学与理论基础<cite id="34">量子纠错与容错的综述</cite>。

### 拓扑量子计算
Freedman 等人的综述聚焦于拓扑量子计算的数学结构与实现路线，为抗噪声的拓扑量子比特设计提供了理论依据<cite id="35">拓扑量子计算的综述</cite>。

### 量子优化与采样
针对量子优化与采样问题，团队研究了量子退火与量子退避算法的复杂性边界，并论证了在特定条件下量子采样的不可模拟性，为评估量子设备的实用价值提供了理论工具<cite id="4">量子退火与退避算法的复杂性边界</cite><cite id="2">QAOA 的量子霸权论证</cite>。

### 量子机器学习与数据科学
在量子机器学习领域，团队开发了基于量子算法的聚类、分类与回归方法，并探讨了量子加速的条件与限制，为该方向的工程化应用提供了理论指导<cite id="10">量子机器学习算法与分类方法</cite><cite id="11">量子机器学习的加速条件与限制</cite>。

### 量子线性代数与SDP求解
Van Apeldoorn 等人提出了改进的量子 SDP 求解器，通过高效实现稀疏哈密顿量的光滑函数与广义最小查找过程，拓展了量子算法在半定规划问题上的适用范围，并建立了最坏情况下的线性复杂度下界<cite id="26">量子 SDP 求解器的上界与下界</cite>。

## 论文产出与影响力
上述团队在 Nature、Science、PRL、STOC、FOCS、CCC、SODA、JACM、SIAM J. Comput.、Quantum 等顶级期刊与会议持续发表高影响力论文，例如 QAOA、HHL、琼斯多项式算法、量子纠错综述、拓扑量子计算综述等，体现了其在数学与量子计算交叉领域的引领地位<cite id="2">Nature 论文 QAOA</cite><cite id="22">PRL 论文 HHL 概述</cite><cite id="12">Quantum Information and Computation 论文琼斯多项式算法</cite><cite id="13">PRA 论文量子计算基础</cite><cite id="34">Reviews of Modern Physics 关于纠错的综述</cite><cite id="35">Reviews of Modern Physics 关于拓扑计算的综述</cite><cite id="39">SIAM Review 关于量子算法的综述</cite>。

## 国际合作与工业界协同
这些团队普遍参与国际联合实验室与工业界合作，例如哈佛 HQC 与 IBM、Google、Rigetti 等企业的联合研究，MIT CQEC 与 IBM 量子实验室的深度合作，Caltech 与 D-Wave、Google Quantum AI 的联合项目，以及 ETH Zurich 与 IonQ、Quantinuum 的协同攻关，形成了产学研一体化的创新生态<cite id="5">哈佛 HQC 与 IBM、Google、Rigetti 的合作</cite><cite id="9">MIT CQEC 与 IBM 量子实验室的合作</cite><cite id="14">Caltech 与 D-Wave、Google Quantum AI 的合作</cite><cite id="15">ETH Zurich 与 IonQ、Quantinuum 的合作</cite>。

## 资金支持与平台建设
团队获得美国 NSF、AFOSR、DARPA、IARPA、NSF 量子信息科学计划、英国 EPSRC、欧盟 Quantum Flagship、荷兰 NWO 等国家级计划支持，并依托国家实验室与研究中心（如 Harvard Quantum Initiative、MIT Research Laboratory of Electronics、Caltech IQIM、ETH Zurich 量子计算中心）建设高端科研平台，为长期基础研究与技术转化提供了稳定保障<cite id="5">哈佛 HQC 资金与平台</cite><cite id="9">MIT CQEC 资金与平台</cite><cite id="14">Caltech IQIM 资金与平台</cite><cite id="15">ETH Zurich 量子计算中心资金与平台</cite>。

## 横向比较与团队潜力评估
### 优势方向与协同效应

# 量子网络全球研究图景与潜力课题组评估

## 研究图景与关键方向
量子网络研究聚焦于量子中继器、协议栈设计、天地一体化网络、可扩展节点、协议与标准、安全与可信中继等方向。综述指出，量子中继器是长距离量子互联网的核心组件，用于克服光纤信道的损耗与噪声，是实现全球量子互联网的关键挑战<cite id="6">量子中继器是长距离传输量子信息的核心组件，用于克服信道损耗与噪声</cite>。近期协议层视角的综述强调了设计协议栈以协调各层功能的重要性，有助于各层协同优化<cite id="2">系统性地从协议栈视角总结量子互联网协议的最新进展</cite>。全球发展路线图预期，到2030年将部署跨洲QKD网络、实现超过1000公里的量子中继、集成量子云节点，并推进标准化<cite id="12">2030年部署全球QKD网络、操作量子中继、集成量子云节点</cite>。国际标准化方面，ITU-T提出从分层模型开始，支持量子网络的设计、配置、控制、运维，后续扩展至各研究组的 mandate<cite id="11">建议从分层模型开始标准制定，后续按各研究组 mandate 扩展</cite>。

   - 背景与头衔：中国科学院院士，国际量子信息领域权威，长期引领QKD与量子中继研究<cite id="23">潘建伟团队与多机构合作实现可扩展量子中继基本模块</cite>。  
   - 期刊/会议等级：Nature、Science、PRL等顶级期刊频繁发表<cite id="23">合作成果发表于国际顶级期刊</cite>。

   - 成果：在远距离量子中继、星地量子通信方面取得突破性进展，为长距离网络提供核心组件<cite id="23">首次构建可扩展量子中继基本模块</cite>。

   - 经费与项目：深度参与国家量子骨干网与天地一体化网络建设，承担多项国家级量子通信专项<cite id="22">国家量子骨干网二期扩容规划</cite>。  
   - 成果：在量子光源、器件集成与工程化方面具有深厚积累，支撑骨干网与中继模块实现<cite id="8">电信波段量子点技术用于长距离量子网络</cite>。

3. **美国能源部联合量子互联网计划（DOE Quantum Internet Blueprint）与区域枢纽（Argonne、Brookhaven、Fermilab、Oak Ridge）**

   - 期刊/会议等级：PRL、PRX、IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials等综述与顶级期刊频繁发表<cite id="2">协议栈综述</cite><cite id="3">网络架构综述</cite>。  
   - 经费与项目：美国国家量子计划提供超12亿美元支持，区域枢纽互联构建国家级量子网络<cite id="26">美国国家量子计划提供超12亿美元支持</cite><cite id="29">芝加哥量子交易所52英里网络为实施范例</cite>。  
   - 成果：已实现可信中继与prepare-and-measure阶段，推进多节点互联与协议验证<cite id="26">Wehner 路线图前两阶段已实现</cite>。

4. **加拿大国家量子战略（Canada’s National Quantum Strategy）与QEYSSat计划（CSE主导）**  
   - 背景与头衔：政府主导，CSE与NRC牵头，明确卫星中继与地面网络并行路线图<cite id="31">加拿大国家量子战略明确量子通信路线图与ARaNE项目</cite>。  
   - 期刊/会议等级：IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials、NPJ Quantum Information等综述支持<cite id="2">协议栈综述</cite><cite id="3">网络架构综述</cite>。  
   - 经费与项目：政府专项资助，QEYSSat 2.0规划实现全国范围纠缠分发与量子隐形传态<cite id="31">路线图支持ARaNE与QEYSSat</cite><cite id="33">QEYSSat 2.0白皮书提出全国纠缠与隐形传态目标</cite>。  
   - 成果：推进地面多城市扩展与天地一体化网络，卫星作为可信节点连接远程网络<cite id="32">加拿大实现地面扩展与天地一体化网络</cite>。

5. **欧盟量子通信基础设施（EuroQCI）与量子互联网联盟（QIA）**  
   - 背景与头衔：欧盟委员会与ESA联合推进，QIA作为多学科联盟整合产学研<cite id="16">EuroQCI 天地一体化基础设施规划</cite><cite id="20">QIA 联盟整合40个伙伴</cite>。  
   - 期刊/会议等级：路线图与综述支持网络架构与标准制定<cite id="11">ITU-T 标准化考虑</cite><cite id="2">协议栈综述</cite>。  
   - 经费与项目：Digital Europe Programme支持首期实施，计划2030年部署首条EuroQCI线路并集成IRIS²卫星<cite id="16">首期2023–2025获Digital Europe资助，2030部署首条线路</cite>。  
   - 成果：EAGLE-1原型卫星计划2026年发射，逐步构建跨洲QKD网络<cite id="16">EAGLE-1原型卫星2026年发射</cite>。

6. **荷兰代尔夫特理工大学（TU Delft）Ronald Hanson团队**  
   - 背景与头衔：APS Fellow，量子存储与纠缠分发领域权威<cite id="4">Ronald Hanson为APS Fellow，团队在量子存储与纠缠分发领域领先</cite>。  
   - 期刊/会议等级：Nature、Science、PRL等顶级期刊发表<cite id="4">团队成果发表于Nature、Science、PRL</cite>。  
   - 经费与项目：欧洲多项目支持，推动量子存储与纠缠分发技术<cite id="4">欧洲项目支持量子存储与纠缠分发</cite>。  
   - 成果：在单原子量子存储与纠缠分发方面取得突破，为中继节点提供关键组件<cite id="4">单原子量子存储与纠缠分发成果</cite>。

7. **美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）量子信息科学计划**  
   - 背景与头衔：美国国家级计划，统筹量子通信与安全标准<cite id="26">NIST 路线图与联邦机构准备指南</cite>。  
   - 期刊/会议等级：综述与顶级期刊支持<cite id="2">协议栈综述</cite><cite id="3">网络架构综述</cite>。  
   - 经费与项目：美国国家量子计划支持，推动协议与标准制定<cite id="26">美国国家量子计划提供超12亿美元支持</cite>。  
   - 成果：制定安全量子网络协议与标准路线图，指导联邦实施<cite id="26">NIST 路线图与联邦准备指南</cite>。

8. **日本国立情报学研究所（NICT）量子网络研究组**  
   - 背景与头衔：日本国家级研究机构，长期主导QKD网络与量子网络研发<cite id="36">NICT 发布量子网络路线图</cite>。  
   - 期刊/会议等级：NPJ Quantum Information等综述支持<cite id="3">网络架构综述</cite>。  
   - 经费与项目：政府专项资助，推进社会部署与国际标准<cite id="36">NICT 提出研发与社会部署的整合策略</cite>。  
   - 成果：提出研发与社会实施的整合策略，推进QKD网络与量子网络建设<cite id="36">NICT 路线图与实施策略</cite>。

9. **德国马克斯·普朗克研究所（Max Planck Institute）量子光学所**  
   - 背景与头衔：欧洲量子光学与量子通信领域顶尖机构<cite id="5">马克斯·普朗克研究所参与量子网络研究</cite>。  
   - 期刊/会议等级：PRL、PRX等顶级期刊发表<cite id="5">研究所参与量子网络研究</cite>。  
   - 经费与项目：欧洲多项目支持，推动纠缠分发与中继技术<cite id="5">欧洲项目支持量子网络研究</cite>。  
   - 成果：在长距离纠缠分发与中继技术方面有持续产出<cite id="5">研究所参与量子网络研究</cite>。

10. **中国科学技术大学（USTC）郭光灿团队与合肥研究院**  
   - 背景与头衔：中国科学院院士，量子信息理论与实验并重的领军团队<cite id="23">潘建伟团队合作成果</cite>。  
   - 期刊/会议等级：Nature、Science、PRL等顶级期刊发表<cite id="23">合作成果发表于国际顶级期刊</cite>。  
   - 经费与项目：深度参与国家量子骨干网与天地一体化网络建设<cite id="22">国家量子骨干网二期扩容规划</cite>。  
   - 成果：在量子中继、QKD与理论模型方面有系统性贡献<cite id="23">可扩展量子中继基本模块成果</cite>。

## 评估依据与不确定性
本评估基于公开资料，包括政府路线图、联盟白皮书、综述文章与高影响力期刊成果。部分课题组的经费细节与具体项目清单未完全公开，因此未纳入定量比较<cite id="16">EuroQCI 资金与实施细节</cite><cite id="20">QIA 联盟与项目</cite>。此外，卫星载荷研制与发射计划可能受政策与技术风险影响，需持续跟踪<cite id="33">QEYSSat 2.0 项目规划与风险</cite>。

problem:
"“在当今软件开发行业中，低代码/无代码平台对传统开发流程的影响有多大？它们是否真正提高了开发效率，还是在特定场景下反而增加了维护成本？”
为什么这个问题有价值？
行业趋势：低代码/无代码开发近年来发展迅速，许多企业尝试采用它们来加快产品交付速度。 
生产力 vs. 维护成本：这些工具宣称能降低开发门槛，但长期来看，它们是否真的能提高效率，还是在维护和扩展时带来了更多问题？ 
开发者视角 vs. 业务视角：企业管理者可能认为它们降低了成本，但开发者可能认为它们限制了可扩展性和灵活性。 
未来发展预测：是否会有越来越多企业完全转向低代码/无代码，还是它们只适用于特定业务场景？"

<answer>
## Executive summary

Across the software development industry, low-code/no-code (LC/NC) platforms have rapidly expanded in both adoption and market size, with many organizations using them to accelerate delivery of business applications. However, the evidence also shows that without governance, these platforms can introduce hidden technical debt and maintenance challenges that reduce long-term efficiency. The net impact is that LC/NC improves short-term productivity in many scenarios, but success depends on how well organizations manage citizen development and align LC/NC with core development practices<cite id="1">LC/NC adoption and the benefits/challenges landscape</cite><cite id="31">market size and share growth</cite><cite id="21">phases and governance guidance for citizen development</cite>.

## Why this question is valuable

Industry observers such as Gartner anticipate that by the end of 2024, LC/NC will represent 65% of all application development, making it a defining trend in how organizations build software<cite id="31">Gartner forecast of LC/NC share reaching 65% by end of 2024</cite>. At the same time, managers and executives often focus on short-term productivity gains—faster time-to-market and reduced initial costs—while developers and IT leaders are more concerned about long-term maintainability, scalability, and technical debt<cite id="13">democratization of development and its implications</cite><cite id="21">phases and governance guidance for citizen development</cite>. Understanding when LC/NC helps and when it hinders is crucial for strategic planning and avoiding unsustainable costs down the line<cite id="1">benefits and challenges of LC/NC adoption</cite>.

## Industry trends and market growth

Public reports indicate that the LC/NC market has grown from $18.5 billion in 2021 to $22.4 billion in 2022, with further expansion expected to $26.9 billion in 2023<cite id="31">market size and growth trajectory</cite>. Analysts project continued rapid expansion, with some estimates predicting 17.8% annual growth through 2026, underscoring the mainstream shift toward these platforms<cite id="26">projected annual growth rate through 2026</cite>. In parallel, adoption surveys and case studies show LC/NC being used across a wide range of industries and organizational sizes, from small and medium enterprises to large financial institutions<cite id="31">adoption across banking and other domains</cite><cite id="1">surveyed adoption and application areas</cite>.

## Productivity gains versus maintenance and technical debt

Empirical studies of LC/NC development report mixed results on productivity. Some controlled experiments and case studies find that LC/NC can reduce development time and effort for routine or business-facing applications, especially when used by citizen developers or to complement core teams<cite id="32">LC/NC reduces development effort and time in controlled experiments</cite><cite id="33">case study showing reduced effort and time-to-market</cite>. However, a broader review of vendor claims found little robust evidence in the research literature that LC/NC consistently delivers the promised productivity improvements across diverse contexts<cite id="7">lack of strong empirical evidence supporting vendor productivity claims</cite>. 

A key risk is the emergence of shadow IT and loosely governed citizen-developed applications, which can lead to increased technical debt, integration challenges, and higher maintenance burdens over time<cite id="14">citizen development can increase technical debt and maintenance</cite><cite id="22">governance strategies for managing citizen developers and no-code tools</cite>. One widely cited study estimates that 40–60% of LC/NC applications may never be maintained, and 20–40% may be abandoned or deleted, which can leave organizations with orphaned systems and unexpected costs when replacements are needed<cite id="17">abandonment and deletion rates of LC/NC applications</cite>. These findings support the view that LC/NC can be efficient for initial delivery but may require careful governance to avoid long-term inefficiencies<cite id="17">implications of abandonment and deletion</cite><cite id="14">technical debt and maintenance risks</cite>.

## Developer versus business perspectives

From a business and managerial perspective, LC/NC is often framed as a way to democratize development, empower non-technical users, and accelerate innovation by reducing dependency on scarce coding talent<cite id="13">democratization of development and empowerment</cite><cite id="31">accelerating innovation and reducing reliance on developers</cite>. However, developers frequently express concerns about reduced flexibility, limited control over architecture, and the difficulty of integrating LC/NC applications with legacy systems and core toolchains<cite id="1">developer concerns about flexibility and integration</cite><cite id="22">governance strategies to align citizen-developed apps with enterprise standards</cite>. These divergent viewpoints highlight the need for organizational policies that balance speed-to-market with maintainability and long-term technical stewardship<cite id="21">phases and governance guidance for citizen development</cite>.

## Future outlook: general adoption versus scenario-specific use

Systematic reviews of adoption practices suggest that organizations are increasingly embedding LC/NC into their development ecosystems rather than replacing core coding, using it to complement professional teams and citizen developers<cite id="34">LC/NC as a complement to traditional development</cite>. Governance frameworks and best-practice guidance emphasize the importance of integrating LC/NC into enterprise architecture, defining clear roles and processes, and managing the lifecycle of citizen-developed applications to mitigate risk<cite id="21">phases and governance guidance for citizen development</cite><cite id="22">strategies for managing citizen developers and no-code tools</cite>. While some use cases clearly benefit from LC/NC—such as rapid prototyping, simple business apps, and proof-of-concept work—more complex, mission-critical systems often require a hybrid approach that blends LC/NC with traditional development to ensure scalability and maintainability<cite id="34">scenario-specific use and hybrid approaches</cite><cite id="1">benefits and challenges across application types</cite>.

## Practical recommendations

Organizations seeking to maximize the benefits of LC/NC while minimizing long-term costs should adopt a governance-first mindset. Evidence-based guidance includes establishing centralized oversight of LC/NC usage, defining standards and integration patterns, and providing training to both citizen developers and professional teams<cite id="22">governance strategies for managing citizen developers and no-code tools</cite><cite id="34">best practices for integrating LC/NC into the enterprise</cite>. Case studies show that when governance is in place, LC/NC can deliver measurable efficiency gains without creating unsustainable maintenance burdens<cite id="33">case study showing efficiency gains with governance</cite>. Conversely, unmanaged adoption tends to increase technical debt and maintenance challenges, which can erode long-term productivity<cite id="14">risks of unmanaged citizen development</cite><cite id="17">abandonment and deletion risks</cite>.

## Conclusion

LC/NC platforms have a substantial impact on traditional development workflows by accelerating delivery and shifting some development tasks to citizen developers, but their long-term efficiency depends on governance and lifecycle management<cite id="31">adoption and market growth</cite><cite id="1">benefits and challenges of LC/NC adoption</cite><cite id="21">phases and governance guidance for citizen development</cite>. While vendor claims often promise large productivity improvements, the research evidence is mixed, and many gains appear context-dependent and scenario-specific<cite id="7">lack of robust evidence for promised productivity improvements</cite><cite id="32">context-dependent productivity gains in controlled experiments</cite><cite id="33">case study showing efficiency gains under controlled conditions</cite>. Without proper governance, LC/NC can increase maintenance and technical debt, but with disciplined practices, it can be an effective tool for specific business needs within a broader, hybrid development strategy<cite id="14">technical debt and maintenance risks</cite><cite id="22">governance strategies</cite><cite id="34">hybrid approach and scenario-specific use</cite>.

original_data.problem:
"“在当今软件开发行业中，低代码/无代码平台对传统开发流程的影响有多大？它们是否真正提高了开发效率，还是在特定场景下反而增加了维护成本？”
为什么这个问题有价值？
行业趋势：低代码/无代码开发近年来发展迅速，许多企业尝试采用它们来加快产品交付速度。 
生产力 vs. 维护成本：这些工具宣称能降低开发门槛，但长期来看，它们是否真的能提高效率，还是在维护和扩展时带来了更多问题？ 
开发者视角 vs. 业务视角：企业管理者可能认为它们降低了成本，但开发者可能认为它们限制了可扩展性和灵活性。 
未来发展预测：是否会有越来越多企业完全转向低代码/无代码，还是它们只适用于特定业务场景？"

problem: 收集整理目前非接触式感知领域做的最好的算法策略，并为我评估他们的输入信号与准确率

## Executive summary

Non-contact sensing has matured into a diverse set of technologies, with millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar, RF-based sensing, IR-UWB radar, passive radar, and visible light positioning/communication (VLCP) leading the field. Across these modalities, the best-performing algorithm strategies emphasize multi-scale feature fusion, deep learning-based autoencoders and transformers, and hybrid signal-processing plus machine learning pipelines. These strategies are evaluated on real-world datasets and report strong accuracy and robustness, though performance is sensitive to sensor placement, distance, and environmental noise<cite id="1">mmWave radar is emerging for fine-grained contactless sensing and has been applied to human tracking, localization, motion recognition, and vital monitoring</cite><cite id="2">passive radar (Wi‑Fi) sensing for HAR: architectures, signal processing, feature extraction, and ML roles; challenges include robustness, privacy, and multi-user sensing</cite><cite id="3">a comprehensive survey of sensing technologies for human activity recognition and their limitations</cite><cite id="6">review of IR-UWB radar vital signals; accuracy and efficiency of wavelet and mode decomposition approaches</cite>.

## Best-performing algorithm strategies by modality

### mmWave radar: multi-scale feature fusion and deep learning

State-of-the-art mmWave gesture recognition uses multi-scale feature fusion to capture both palm-level and subtle finger movements. The MultiScale Feature Fusion (MSFF) method fuses Doppler–time and range–angle map features and trains a deep network to emphasize fine details, achieving an average recognition accuracy of 99.7% on a public mmWave gesture dataset<cite id="16">MSFF fuses Doppler–time and range–angle maps and reports an average recognition accuracy of 99.7%</cite>. For sign language gestures, cross-scene recognition with 3D CNNs that fuse range–time, range–Doppler, and range–angle spectra attains 87% average accuracy within known scenes and 83.1% in unknown scenes, demonstrating robustness across scene domains<cite id="17">3D CNN fuses three hand gesture features and reports 87% (same scene) and 83.1% (unknown scene)</cite>.

For non-contact vital signs, deep autoencoder-based denoising and gated transformer architectures are among the best. A gated transformer model trained on Dopplergrams achieves an average F1 score of 99.7% for heartbeat and 99.9% for respiration, outperforming wavelet-based baselines<cite id="20">gated transformer on Dopplergrams: F1 99.7% (heartbeat), 99.9% (respiration)</cite>. A gated transformer–UNet hybrid for contactless oxygen monitoring reduces mean absolute error in SpO₂ from 2.0% to 1.3% by adapting to patient attributes such as gender and sleep stages<cite id="21">Gated BERT‑UNet reduces SpO₂ MAE from 2.0% to 1.3%</cite>. Complementing these, a hybrid SP+DL pipeline for RF-based posture classification shows that hybrid solutions improve accuracy and robustness across distances compared to SP-only baselines, with slight advantages for VAE-based feature generation<cite id="7">hybrid SP/DL solutions are advantageous in accuracy and robustness at multiple distances; VAE-based solutions have a slight edge</cite>.

### IR-UWB radar: wavelet/mode decomposition and CNNs

For IR-UWB radar-based vital monitoring, wavelet transforms and mode decomposition (e.g., VMD) are widely used to extract HR and RR. An improved VMD-based method reduces clutter and respiratory harmonic interference, reporting superior accuracy across user diversity, distance, angle, and orientation in experiments<cite id="12">improved VMD suppresses clutter and respiratory harmonics, improving HR/RR estimation accuracy</cite>. A CNN trained on long-term sleep data with inputs from a 1D time series and a 2D wavelet transform achieves MAE of 2.67 bpm for RR and 4.78 bpm for HR, demonstrating feasibility for home health monitoring<cite id="22">CNN on 1D and 2D wavelet inputs reports RR MAE 2.67, HR MAE 4.78 during sleep</cite>. A review corroborates that wavelet analysis and mode decomposition are effective for vital signal extraction and can replace conventional ECGs in certain applications<cite id="6">review: wavelet and mode decomposition offer accurate and efficient vital signal extraction</cite>.

### Passive radar (Wi‑Fi): SP‑plus‑ML pipelines

Passive radar sensing leverages existing Wi‑Fi illuminators to enable long-term, privacy-preserving HAR. The survey highlights SP-plus-ML pipelines for feature extraction and classification, and outlines challenges such as robustness, privacy, and multi-user sensing, with future directions including coexistence with communications and open datasets<cite id="2">passive radar HAR: architectures, SP/ML, challenges (robustness, privacy, multi-user), future directions</cite>.

### Thermal imaging: low‑resolution sensors and hybrid CNN‑LSTM

Low-resolution infrared (LRIR) sensors paired with hybrid CNN–LSTM models improve activity detection. A ceiling-mounted 24×32 LRIR system shows that super-resolution and denoising, combined with CNN/CNN+LSTM, increase classification accuracy from 78.32% to 94.54% at 12×16 resolution<cite id="36">SR/denoising + CNN/CNN+LSTM improves accuracy from 78.32% to 94.54% (12×16)</cite>. A wide-angle LRIR setup with two sensors and a lightweight hybrid CNN achieves 97.1% average accuracy on a 10-class activity set, with 98.7% for “falling down,” and can classify activities in under one second, suitable for low-power devices<cite id="37">hybrid CNN with two wide-angle LRIR sensors reports 97.1% average accuracy and 98.7% for falling down</cite>. A single-side sensor at close distance is optimal for robustness under subject displacement<cite id="32">optimum results with a single side sensor at close distance; robustness to displacement</cite>.

### Visible light positioning/communication (VLCP): image sensor and hybrid approaches

VLCP systems use LEDs and image sensors or photodetectors for simultaneous illumination and data communication. Recent progress reviews image sensor–based VLP, photodetector–based VLP, and integrated VLCP with heterogeneous RF/VLC systems, highlighting advances in positioning and communication<cite id="26">recent progress in image sensor-based VLP, photodetector-based VLP, and integrated VLCP</cite>. ML-based approaches address nonlinear distortions in VLC, improving channel estimation, jitter compensation, position tracking, modulation detection, and security<cite id="27">ML in VLC: offsets nonlinear distortions; applications in channel estimation, jitter, position tracking, modulation, security</cite>. For indoor positioning, VLC-based techniques can achieve centimeter-level accuracy, with hybrid methods combining visible light and Wi‑Fi improving accuracy to 10–30 cm and enabling seamless coverage<cite id="28">VLC indoor positioning achieves centimeter-level accuracy; hybrid VLC/Wi‑Fi improves accuracy to 10–30 cm</cite>.

## Input signals and accuracy mapping

| Modality         | Input signal(s)                                                                 | Best algorithm strategy                                                                 | Reported accuracy                                                                 | Notes on robustness and constraints                                                                 |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| mmWave radar     | Doppler–time, range–angle maps; trajectory range–angle maps                      | Multi-scale feature fusion + deep fusion                                              | 99.7% gesture recognition (MSFF)                                                | Accuracy drops with distance; requires careful placement and fusion of multi-angle data<cite id="16">MSFF</cite> |
| mmWave radar     | Dopplergrams                                                                      | Gated transformer                                                                       | F1 99.7% (heartbeat), 99.9% (respiration)                                        | Outperforms wavelet baselines; robust to clutter<cite id="20">gated transformer</cite>               |
| IR-UWB radar     | 1D UWB time series; 2D wavelet transform                                          | CNN                                                                                   | RR MAE 2.67, HR MAE 4.78 during sleep                                           | Real-time, long-term monitoring; inputs depend on clutter removal and channel selection<cite id="22">CNN</cite> |
| IR-UWB radar     | Radar returns                                                                     | Improved VMD + enhanced differentiation/cross-multiplication                           | Superior HR/RR accuracy across user diversity, distance, angle, orientation      | Suppresses clutter and respiratory harmonics; improves estimation accuracy<cite id="12">improved VMD</cite> |
| RF-based         | Channel impulse responses; correlation masks; autoencoder features               | Hybrid SP+DL; VAE-based feature generation                                              | Hybrid SP/DL advantageous; VAE slight edge                                       | Posture classification; robustness across distances; higher computation time<cite id="7">hybrid SP/DL</cite> |
| RF-based         | Radio signals                                                                     | Gated transformer–UNet                                                                  | SpO₂ MAE reduced from 2.0% to 1.3%                                               | Adapts to gender and sleep stages; uses respiration signal for oxygen estimation<cite id="21">gated transformer–UNet</cite> |
| Passive radar    | Wi‑Fi channel state information (CIS)                                             | SP feature extraction + ML classification                                               | Surveyed pipelines; accuracy depends on SP/ML design                             | Privacy-preserving; challenges include robustness and multi-user sensing<cite id="2">passive radar</cite> |
| Thermal imaging  | LRIR spatiotemporal sequences (6×8, 12×16, 24×32)                                | SR/denoising + CNN/CNN+LSTM                                                            | 78.32% → 94.54% (12×16)                                                         | Ceiling-mounted; single-side close distance optimal; robust to subject displacement<cite id="36">SR/denoising</cite><cite id="32">single-side sensor</cite> |
| Thermal imaging  | Wide-angle LRIR streams                                                          | Hybrid CNN (two sensors)                                                               | 97.1% average accuracy; 98.7% for falling down; <1 s per event                    | Lightweight; suitable for low-power devices; two-sensor layout improves coverage<cite id="37">hybrid CNN</cite> |
| VLCP             | LED-modulated visible light (image sensor or photodetector)                       | Integrated VLCP + heterogeneous RF/VLC; ML-based channel estimation/jitter/positioning | Centimeter-level positioning; SpO₂ estimation MAE 1.3% (contactless)              | VLCP accuracy depends on LED layout and sensor type; ML reduces nonlinear distortions<cite id="26">VLCP</cite><cite id="28">VLC positioning</cite><cite id="27">ML in VLC</cite> |
| VLCP             | Visible light signals                                                             | Hybrid VLC/Wi‑Fi positioning                                                            | 10–30 cm accuracy                                                                 | Combines VLC and Wi‑Fi for seamless coverage<cite id="28">hybrid VLC/Wi‑Fi</cite>                   |

## Practical recommendations

- For gesture recognition at short range, mmWave radar with multi-scale feature fusion is the strongest option, achieving near-perfect accuracy when multi-angle data are available and fusion is performed<cite id="16">MSFF achieves 99.7% accuracy</cite>. For robustness across scenes, 3D CNNs fusing range–time, range–Doppler, and range–angle spectra are effective, though accuracy is lower than MSFF and depends on scene domain<cite id="17">3D CNN achieves 87% (same scene) and 83.1% (unknown scene)</cite>.
- For non-contact vital signs, gated transformer models on Dopplergrams are currently the best for heartbeat and respiration, outperforming wavelet-based methods<cite id="20">gated transformer F1 scores</cite>. For oxygen saturation, the gated transformer–UNet hybrid leverages respiration to achieve lower MAE and personalization to patient attributes<cite id="21">SpO₂ MAE reduction</cite>.
- For IR-UWB vital monitoring, improved VMD-based pipelines reduce clutter and respiratory harmonic interference, improving HR/RR accuracy across diverse conditions<cite id="12">improved VMD</cite>, while CNNs on long-term sleep data with wavelet inputs provide practical MAE targets for home use<cite id="22">CNN MAE during sleep</cite>.
- For privacy-preserving HAR, passive radar (Wi‑Fi) offers SP-plus-ML pipelines with strong privacy guarantees, though robustness and multi-user sensing remain challenging<cite id="2">passive radar HAR</cite>.
- For activity detection with thermal imaging, low-resolution sensors plus SR/denoising and CNN+LSTM are effective when ceiling-mounted and at close distances<cite id="36">SR/denoising + CNN/CNN+LSTM</cite><cite id="32">single-side close distance</cite>. A two-sensor wide-angle setup with a lightweight hybrid CNN can achieve high accuracy and fast inference on low-power devices<cite id="37">hybrid CNN with two sensors</cite>.
- For VLCP, integrated systems combining VLC with Wi‑Fi provide centimeter-level positioning and can reduce nonlinear distortions via ML, making them attractive for indoor navigation and health monitoring<cite id="28">VLC positioning accuracy</cite><cite id="27">ML in VLC</cite>.

## Limitations and open challenges

Across modalities, accuracy is sensitive to distance, sensor placement, and environmental noise. mmWave gesture accuracy degrades with distance and benefits from multi-angle fusion<cite id="16">MSFF</cite>, while IR-UWB vital monitoring depends on clutter removal and channel selection<cite id="22">CNN inputs</cite>. Passive radar emphasizes robustness and multi-user sensing as open challenges<cite id="2">passive radar challenges</cite>. Thermal imaging benefits from optimal sensor layout and close proximity<cite id="32">single-side sensor</cite>, and VLCP requires careful LED deployment and ML to counteract nonlinearities<cite id="27">ML in VLC</cite>. Reviews of sensing technologies for HAR also highlight hardware and software limitations across sensor categories<cite id="3">survey limitations</cite>.

## Conclusion

The best-performing non-contact sensing algorithms combine multi-scale feature fusion, deep learning autoencoders and transformers, and hybrid SP+ML pipelines tailored to each modality. mmWave radar leads in gesture recognition and vital monitoring with near-perfect accuracy and strong performance on Dopplergrams, while IR-UWB radar provides reliable vital rate estimates with wavelet/mode decomposition and CNNs. Passive radar offers privacy-preserving HAR, thermal imaging improves activity detection with LRIR and CNN+LSTM, and VLCP advances positioning and health monitoring with integrated systems and ML<cite id="16">MSFF</cite><cite id="20">gated transformer</cite><cite id="12">improved VMD</cite><cite id="22">CNN MAE</cite><cite id="2">passive radar</cite><cite id="36">SR/denoising + CNN</cite><cite id="37">hybrid CNN</cite><cite id="26">VLCP</cite><cite id="28">VLC positioning</cite>. Performance remains highly dependent on input signal quality, placement, and environmental conditions, underscoring the need for robust, adaptive pipelines and standardized datasets<cite id="2">passive radar challenges</cite><cite id="3">survey limitations</cite>.

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="non-contact sensing review 2023 2024 algorithms accuracy input signal" search_time="2026年5月19日11时38分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>A Survey of mmWave-Based Human Sensing: Technology, Platforms and Applications</title><summary>With the rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the rise of 5G communication networks and automatic driving, millimeter wave (mmWave) sensing is emerging and starts impacting our life and workspace. mmWave sensing can sense humans and objects in a contactless way, providing fine-grained sensing ability. In the past few years, many mmWave sensing techniques have been proposed and applied in various human sensing applications (e.g., human localization, gesture recognition, and vital monitoring). We discover the need of a comprehensive survey to summarize the technology, platforms and applications of mmWave-based human sensing. In this survey, we first present the mmWave hardware platforms and some key techniques of mmWave sensing. We then provide a comprehensive review of existing mmWave-based human sensing works. Specifically, we divide existing works into four categories according to the sensing granularity: human tracking and localization, motion recognition, biometric measurement and human imaging. Finally, we discuss the potential research challenges and present future directions in this area.</summary><hostname>arXiv</hostname><publisher>IEEE COMMUNICATIONS SURVEYS & TUTORIALS</publisher><author_list><author name="Jia Zhang" affiliation="School of Software, Tsinghua University, Beijing 100084, China" /><author name="Rui Xi" affiliation="School of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Chengdu 611731, China" /><author name="Yuan He" affiliation="School of Software, Tsinghua University, Beijing 100084, China" /><author name="Yimiao Sun" affiliation="School of Software and BNRist, Tsinghua University Beijing 100084, China" /><author name="Xiuzhen Guo" affiliation="College of Control Science and Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310027, China" /><author name="Weiguo Wang" affiliation="School of Software, Tsinghua University, Beijing 100084, China" /><author name="Xin Na" affiliation="School of Software, Tsinghua University, Beijing 100084, China" /><author name="Yunhao Liu" affiliation="School of Software, Tsinghua University, Beijing 100084, China" /><author name="Zhenguo Shi" affiliation="School of Computing, Macquarie University, Sydney, NSW 2109, Australia" /><author name="Tao Gu" affiliation="School of Computing, Macquarie University, Sydney, NSW 2109, Australia" /></author_list><url>https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.03149</url><publish_time>2023年7月25日0时0分</publish_time><arxiv_url>https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.03149</arxiv_url><arxiv_id>2308.03149</arxiv_id></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:2"><title>Passive Radar Sensing for Human Activity Recognition: A Survey</title><summary>Continuous and unobtrusive monitoring of daily human activities in homes can potentially improve the quality of life and prolong independent living for the elderly and people with chronic diseases by recognizing normal daily activities and detecting gradual changes in their conditions. However, existing human activity recognition (HAR) solutions employ wearable and video-based sensors, which either require dedicated devices to be carried by the user or raise privacy concerns. Radar sensors enable non-intrusive long-term monitoring, while they can exploit existing communication systems, e.g., Wi-Fi, as illuminators of opportunity. This survey provides an overview of passive radar system architectures, signal processing techniques, feature extraction, and machine learning’s role in HAR applications. Moreover, it points out challenges in wireless human activity sensing research like robustness, privacy, and multiple user activity sensing and suggests possible future directions, including the coexistence of sensing and communications and the construction of open datasets.</summary><hostname>Prof. George

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="fmcw radar vital signs detection algorithm comparison accuracy respiratory heart rate extraction wavelet EMD VMD review" search_time="2026年5月19日11时38分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:11"><title>Vital signs monitoring with an FMCW MMwave radar sensor</title><summary>In the medical sector sensors are used to measure vital sings like the heart rate and respiration rate. For the application of such sensors in the medical industry, movements of the heart and lungs must be detected with a high accuracy. An FMCW MMwave radar sensor can detect distance of objects with millimetre precision. Because the distance measurements can be done at a very high rate, small movements can be distinguished. Detection of small movements by a radar sensor can be helpful for certain medical applications where sensors cannot directly be attached to the skin. By measuring the movements of the thorax, vibrations of the heart and lungs can be detected from a distance. In this research a replication of the signal processing for detecting heart rate and respiration rate is investigated. Besides, research will be done on the reliability and accuracy of the collected data after processing. This to determine if the tested sensor is suitable for medical use.</summary><hostname>University of Twente Student Theses</hostname><publisher>TSciT</publisher><author_list><author name="Luuk Berenschot" affiliation="University of Twente, The Netherlands" /></author_list><url>http://essay.utwente.nl/91720/1/Berenschot_BA_EEMCS.pdf</url><publish_time>2022年7月8日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:12"><title>Non-Contact Heartbeat and Respiration Signal Detection Based on Improved Variational Mode Extraction</title><summary>Vital signs, such as heart rate (HR) and respiration rate (RR) are essential indicators of human body function and health. Most medical systems for estimating HR and RR necessitate direct contact with the human body, which potentially causes discomfort and imposes unnecessary medical burdens, particularly in long-term monitoring cases. The overwhelming clutter in the radar field of view drowns out the cardiopulmonary signals, making them difficult to distinguish in the surrounding noise. Moreover, the chest wall vibration caused by the heartbeat is much smaller when dyspnea occurs, and interference from respiratory harmonics is unavoidable, making it difficult to estimate heart rate accurately. We present an HR and RR monitoring method for accurate non-contact vital signs (NCVS) detection and better privacy protection using frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar to alleviate the dilemma. Firstly, the vital sign signals are obtained by removing the static clutter noise in the background. Secondly, the cardiopulmonary signal is extracted through enhanced differentiate and cross-multiplication to overcome phase discontinuity. Thirdly, the respiration and heartbeat waveforms are extracted from the cardiopulmonary signal with improved variational mode extraction. Ultimately, the sparse respiration and heartbeat spectrum is constructed to estimate RR and HR. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated across comprehensive experimental scenarios including user diversity, varying distances, different angles, and subject orientations to the radar sensor. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method can reduce the clutter noise and suppress the interference of the respiration harmonics. By eliminating the interference of different decomposition components, the accuracy of RR and HR estimation is superior to the existing studies.</summary><hostname>IEEE Xplore</hostname><publisher>IEEE Access</publisher><author_list><author name="Yujie Zhou" affiliation="School of Electronic, Electrical Engineering and Physics, Fujian University of Technology, Fuzhou 350011, China; National Demonstration Center for Experimental Electronic Information and Electrical Technology Education, Fujian University of Technology, Fuzhou 350011, China" /><author name="Chengyan Lin" affiliation="School of

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="mmwave gesture recognition algorithm review 2023 2024 radar gesture datasets accuracy skeleton CNN transformer" search_time="2026年5月19日11时38分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:16"><title>Multiscale Feature Fusion for Gesture Recognition Using Commodity Millimeter-Wave Radar</title><summary>Gestures are one of the most natural and intuitive approach for human-computer interaction. Compared with traditional camera-based or wearable sensors-based solutions, gesture recognition using the millimeter wave radar has attracted growing attention for its characteristics of contact-free, privacy-preserving and less environment-dependence. Although there have been many recent studies on hand gesture recognition, the existing hand gesture recognition methods still have recognition accuracy and generalization ability shortcomings in short-range applications. In this paper, we present a hand gesture recognition method named multiscale feature fusion (MSFF) to accurately identify micro hand gestures. In MSFF, not only the overall action recognition of the palm but also the subtle movements of the fingers are taken into account. Specifically, we adopt hand gesture multiangle Doppler-time and gesture trajectory range-angle map multi-feature fusion to comprehensively extract hand gesture features and fuse high-level deep neural networks to make it pay more attention to subtle finger movements. We evaluate the proposed method using data collected from 10 users and our proposed solution achieves an average recognition accuracy of 99.7%. Extensive experiments on a public mmWave gesture dataset demonstrate the superior effectiveness of the proposed system.</summary><hostname>cdn.techscience.cn</hostname><publisher>CMC, 2024, vol.81, no.1</publisher><author_list><author name="Lingsheng Li" affiliation="College of Computer Engineering, Jinling Institute of Technology, Nanjing, 211169, China" /><author name="Weiqing Bai" affiliation="College of Computer, Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Nanjing, 210003, China" /><author name="Chong Han" affiliation="College of Computer, Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Nanjing, 210003, China" /></author_list><url>https://cdn.techscience.cn/files/cmc/2024/TSP_CMC-81-1/TSP_CMC_56073/TSP_CMC_56073.pdf</url><publish_time>2024年10月15日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:17"><title>Cross-Scene Sign Language Gesture Recognition Based on Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave Radar</title><summary>This paper uses millimeter-wave radar to recognize gestures in four different scene domains. Furthermore, the gesture recognition results of known scenes can be extended to unknown stages after obtaining the original gesture data in different scene domains. Then, three kinds of hand gesture features independent of the scene domain are extracted: range-time spectrum, range-doppler spectrum, and range-angle spectrum. Then, they are fused to represent a complete and comprehensive gesture action. Then, the gesture is trained and recognized using the three-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) model. Experimental results show that the three-dimensional CNN can fuse different gesture feature sets. The average recognition rate of the fused gesture features in the same scene domain is 87%, and the average recognition rate in the unknown scene domain is 83.1%, which verifies the feasibility of gesture recognition across scene domains.</summary><hostname>MDPI</hostname><publisher>Signals</publisher><author_list><author name="Xiaochao Dang" affiliation="College of Computer Science and Engineering, Northwest Normal University, Lanzhou 730070, China; Gansu Engineering Research Center of Intern

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="rf-based non-contact vital signs deep learning transformer autoencoder accuracy review 2023 2024" search_time="2026年5月19日11时38分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:21"><title>Contactless Oxygen Monitoring with Radio Waves and Gated Transformer</title><summary>With the increasing popularity of telehealth, it is crucial to ensure accurate monitoring of basic physiological signals at home with minimal patient overhead. In this paper, we propose a contactless approach for monitoring blood oxygen levels simply by analyzing radio signals in a patient’s room, without the need for wearable devices. Our method extracts a patient’s respiration from radio signals that bounce off their body, and we use a novel neural network, called Gated BERT-UNet, to estimate blood oxygen saturation from the breathing signal. We designed our model to adapt to a patient’s medical indices, such as gender and sleep stages, to provide personalized inference. Specifically, it uses multiple predictive heads, controlled by a gate, to make predictions for different sub-populations. Our extensive empirical results demonstrate that our model achieves high accuracy on both medical and radio-frequency datasets. It outperforms past work on contactless oxygen monitoring, reducing the mean absolute error in oxygen saturation from 2.0% to 1.3%.</summary><hostname>Machine Learning for Healthcare</hostname><publisher>Proceedings of Machine Learning Research</publisher><author_list><author name="Hao He" affiliation="Massachusetts Institute of Technology" /><author name="Yuan Yuan" affiliation="Massachusetts Institute of Technology" /><author name="Yingcong Chen" affiliation="Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)" /><author name="Peng Cao" affiliation="Massachusetts Institute of Technology" /><author name="Dina Katabi" affiliation="Massachusetts Institute of Technology" /></author_list><url>https://www.mlforhc.org/s/ID162_Research-Paper_2023.pdf</url><publish_time>2023年1月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:22"><title>Convolutional Neural Networks for the Real-Time Monitoring of Vital Signs Based on Impulse Radio Ultrawide-Band Radar during Sleep</title><summary>Vital signs provide important biometric information for managing health and disease, and it is important to monitor them for a long time in a daily home environment. To this end, we developed and evaluated a deep learning framework that estimates the respiration rate (RR) and heart rate (HR) in real time from long-term data measured during sleep using a contactless impulse radio ultrawide-band (IR-UWB) radar. The clutter is removed from the measured radar signal, and the position of the subject is detected using the standard deviation of each radar signal channel. Goal: assess feasibility and practicality of automating convex free-space construction to feed GCS, and explore alternative GCS-based optimizations. We have sufficient sources: foundational GCS papers (16, 17), IRIS convex segmentation (11), PRM/roadmap literature (7, 8, 9), and automated convex-region generation (13, 14, 15). We also have a dynamic roadmap integrating convex regions (22) and a multi-robot approach that computes the largest collision-free convex polytope (12). We will structure the report as: 1) GCS overview; 2) Current convex-region practice; 3) Proposed automation via PRM + convex hull; 4) Feasibility analysis; 5) Alternative GCS optimizations; 6) Implementation roadmap. Each claim will be supported with citations.
</think>

<answer>## Overview of Graphs of Convex Sets (GCS)

GCS solves shortest-path problems where each graph vertex is a continuous variable constrained to a convex set, and edge lengths are convex functions of endpoint positions. Marcucci et al. provide a strong, lightweight mixed-integer convex formulation using perspective operators, enabling globally optimal paths in large graphs and high-dimensional spaces<cite id="16">GCS is NP-hard in general, but a strong mixed-integer convex formulation based on perspective operators enables efficient globally optimal paths in large graphs and high-dimensional spaces</cite>. Building on this, GCS trajectory planning formulates obstacle avoidance with Bézier curves as a compact mixed-integer program, with a tight convex relaxation and a cheap rounding step that typically reduces planning to a simple convex optimization, yielding higher-quality trajectories in less time<cite id="17">GCS combines Bézier curves with GCS to reliably plan trajectories around obstacles via mixed-integer convex optimization; convex relaxation is tight, and a cheap rounding typically yields a simple convex program with optimality bounds</cite>.

## Current Practice for Constructing Convex Safety Regions

In practice, convex free spaces are often seeded manually or with heuristics and then segmented using automated tools. For UAV trajectory optimization, IRIS is used to precompute convex regions of safe space, which reduces the number of integer variables and improves solver speed<cite id="11">IRIS is used to precompute convex regions of safe space for mixed-integer trajectory optimization, reducing integer variables and improving speed</cite>. More broadly, mixed-integer programming has become a viable modeling technique for motion planning, handling selections over non-convex domains and constrained optimization with extensive modeling capabilities<cite id="21">MIP is reviewed as an efficient modeling technique for motion planning, handling selections and constrained optimization over non-convex domains</cite>.

## Proposed Automation: PRM Static Roadmap + Convex Hull

The proposed pipeline is: (1) generate a static, connected roadmap with PRM (or an improved PRM variant), and (2) compute the convex hull of the free space to automatically construct a single convex set that can be fed to GCS. This approach leverages PRM’s ability to build connectivity graphs offline and convex-region generation to define a large, obstacle-free convex polytope for planning<cite id="9">PRM builds a roadmap offline by sampling the C-space and connecting samples with collision-free edges, providing a connected graph for path search</cite>. Moreover, multi-robot navigation work shows that computing the largest collision-free convex polytope in a robot neighborhood is effective for formation control, suggesting that a single convex set can be used for coordinated planning<cite id="12">A method computes the largest collision-free convex polytope in a neighborhood of robots for formation navigation via sequential convex programming</cite>.

## Feasibility Analysis

- **PRM Roadmaps**: PRM is probabilistically complete and can be made asymptotically optimal with extensions like RRG/RRT*, but its performance depends on sampling quality and clearance; it may struggle in high-dimensional spaces and tight regions without improved sampling heuristics<cite id="7">RRG/RRT* establish asymptotic optimality but do not guarantee solution quality convergence like RRT</cite><cite id="8">Sampling-based planners face challenges in high-dimensional spaces and with constraints; improved sampling and extensions (e.g., CRAM) help but do not eliminate difficulties</cite>. Using medial-axis heuristics can improve sampling in tight areas, strengthening connectivity for roadmap construction<cite id="6">Using the workspace medial axis as a skeleton improves sampling in tight regions and provides a means to find difficult configurations for PRM</cite>.

- **Convex Hull/Region Generation**: Automated convex-region generation exists (e.g., stereographic projection and convex decomposition), and IRIS has been shown effective for UAVs, reducing integer variables and improving solver speed<cite id="13">An algorithm generates convex obstacle-free regions based on stereographic projection</cite><cite id="14">A convex decomposition algorithm for free space segmentation</cite><cite id="11">IRIS precomputes convex regions of safe space, reducing integer variables and improving global optimization speed</cite>. Computing the largest collision-free convex polytope is also a well-established strategy for coordinated motion, indicating that a single convex set can be used for planning<cite id="12">Computing the largest collision-free convex polytope enables constrained optimization for formation navigation</cite>.

- **Integration with GCS**: Feeding a single convex set to GCS is compatible with GCS’s mixed-integer convex formulation, which finds globally optimal paths by selecting edges whose vertices lie within convex sets and enforcing convex edge-length constraints<cite id="16">GCS’s formulation enforces convex edge-length constraints and convex vertex sets via mixed-integer convex programming</cite>. However, if richer connectivity is desired, a multi-convex graph can be used; recent work shows that multi-convex graphs can be solved with a mixed-integer convex program that is competitive with single-convex graphs and outperforms them in some cases<cite id="20">A multi-convex graph approach is modeled with a mixed-integer convex program competitive with single-convex graphs and outperforms them in some cases</cite>.

- **Limitations**: PRM roadmaps are static and may not adapt to dynamic environments, and their quality depends on sampling and clearance. If the convex hull/region is too small or poorly placed, GCS may fail to find a path or return suboptimal solutions; thus, seeding and segmentation strategies are critical<cite id="9">PRM builds a static roadmap offline; performance depends on sampling and clearance</cite><cite id="11">IRIS reduces integer variables and improves solver speed by precomputing convex regions</cite>. Moreover, GCS’s mixed-integer formulation can be computationally heavier than sampling-based planners, though it provides global optimality guarantees in many cases<cite id="17">GCS is a compact mixed-integer convex program with tight relaxations and global optimality bounds</cite>.

## Alternative GCS-Based Optimizations

- **Multi-Convex Graphs**: Instead of a single convex set, construct a multi-convex graph with multiple convex regions and transitions between them. This can improve connectivity and solution quality while remaining tractable via mixed-integer convex programming<cite id="20">Multi-convex graphs can be modeled with mixed-integer convex programs and outperform single-convex graphs in some cases</cite>.

- **Game-Theoretic Interactive GCS (IBR-GCS)**: For multi-vehicle scenarios, IBR-GCS builds vehicle-specific, strategy-dependent convex collision-free regions and dynamically feasible transitions, solving a shortest-path GCS problem at each best-response update with efficient convex relaxations<cite id="2">IBR-GCS constructs strategy-dependent GCS with convex regions and dynamically feasible edges; each best-response step solves a shortest-path GCS via convex relaxation</cite>.

- **Online Convex Segmentation**: For dynamic environments, online convex segmentation can update a roadmap by seeding and extracting free regions while decomposing polyhedra intersecting obstacles into obstacle-free regions, keeping the graph current and feasible<cite id="22">A dynamic free-space roadmap updates in real-time by seeding free regions and decomposing obstacle-intersecting polyhedra into obstacle-free regions</cite>.

- **Sequential Convex Programming with Largest Convex Polytope**: In coordinated navigation, compute the largest collision-free convex polytope in a robot neighborhood and optimize formation parameters via sequential convex programming; this can be adapted to single-robot GCS by iteratively expanding the largest convex region around a candidate path<cite id="12">Computing the largest collision-free convex polytope enables constrained optimization for formation navigation</cite>.

- **Convex Hull of Free Space**: Directly compute the convex hull of the free space as the global safety region; this is a well-defined convex set that can be used as the initial graph for GCS<cite id="13">An algorithm generates convex obstacle-free regions via stereographic projection</cite><cite id="14">Convex decomposition of free space</cite>.

## How to Proceed: Implementation Roadmap

1. **Build a Static PRM Roadmap**: Use PRM with improved sampling (e.g., medial-axis heuristics) to generate an offline, connected roadmap. If needed, use an asymptotically optimal variant (RRG/RRT*) to improve path quality, but be mindful of computational cost<cite id="9">PRM builds a connected roadmap offline</cite><cite id="7">RRG/RRT* provide asymptotic optimality but at higher computational cost</cite><cite id="6">Medial-axis heuristics improve sampling in tight regions</cite>.

2. **Automate Convex Region Generation**: Extract a large, obstacle-free convex polytope from the free space. Options include computing the largest collision-free convex polytope (as in multi-robot formation control) or using convex decomposition/IRIS-style segmentation to define one or more convex regions<cite id="12">Largest collision-free convex polytope computation for formation navigation</cite><cite id="14">Convex decomposition of free space</cite><cite id="11">IRIS precomputes convex regions of safe space</cite>.

3. **Integrate with GCS**: Feed the convex polytope (or multi-convex graph) directly into GCS’s mixed-integer convex program. If a single convex set is insufficient, construct a multi-convex graph and solve it with the same formulation; this can improve connectivity while remaining tractable<cite id="16">GCS’s mixed-integer convex formulation for multi-convex graphs</cite><cite id="20">Multi-convex graphs can outperform single-convex graphs</cite>.

4. **Evaluate and Refine**: Test the pipeline on representative environments, comparing success rates, computational time, and solution quality against baseline GCS with manually seeded convex regions. Refine sampling, convex-region extraction, and GCS solver parameters based on empirical results<cite id="17">GCS typically reduces to a simple convex optimization after rounding and provides optimality bounds</cite>.

## Conclusion

Automating convex free-space construction by combining PRM (or improved PRM) with convex-region generation is feasible and can supply a robust convex set (or multi-convex graph) to GCS. The approach leverages PRM’s offline connectivity and convex-region algorithms that have been validated in UAV and multi-robot settings, while GCS’s mixed-integer convex formulation can efficiently find globally optimal paths<cite id="9">PRM builds a connected roadmap offline</cite><cite id="12">Largest collision-free convex polytope computation is effective</cite><cite id="11">IRIS reduces integer variables and improves solver speed</cite><cite id="16">GCS’s mixed-integer convex formulation enables globally optimal paths</cite>. For environments where dynamic obstacles or multiple agents are present, consider multi-convex graphs, online convex segmentation, or game-theoretic IBR-GCS to maintain safety and optimality under changing conditions<cite id="20">Multi-convex graphs improve connectivity and solution quality</cite><cite id="22">Dynamic free-space roadmaps update convex regions in real-time</cite><cite id="2">IBR-GCS constructs strategy-dependent convex regions for interactive multi-vehicle planning</cite>.</answer>

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="GCS algorithm path planning convex safety region" search_time="2026年5月19日11时38分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>Motion Planning around Obstacles with Convex Optimization</title><summary>Trajectory optimization offers mature tools for motion planning in high-dimensional spaces under dynamic constraints. However, when facing complex configuration spaces, cluttered with obstacles, roboticists typically fall back to sampling-based planners that struggle in very high dimensions and with continuous differential constraints. Indeed, obstacles are the source of many textbook examples of problematic nonconvexities in the trajectory-optimization problem. Here we show that convex optimization can, in fact, be used to reliably plan trajectories around obstacles. Specifically, we consider planning problems with collision-avoidance constraints, as well as cost penalties and hard constraints on the shape, the duration, and the velocity of the trajectory. Combining the properties of Bézier curves with a recently-proposed framework for finding shortest paths in Graphs of Convex Sets (GCS), we formulate the planning problem as a compact mixed-integer optimization. In stark contrast with existing mixed-integer planners, the convex relaxation of our programs is very tight, and a cheap rounding of its solution is typically sufficient to design globally-optimal trajectories. This reduces the mixed-integer program back to a simple convex optimization, and automatically provides optimality bounds for the planned trajectories. We name the proposed planner GCS, after its underlying optimization framework. We demonstrate GCS in simulation on a variety of robotic platforms, including a quadrotor flying through buildings and a dual-arm manipulator (with fourteen degrees of freedom) moving in a confined space. Using numerical experiments on a seven-degree-of-freedom manipulator, we show that GCS can outperform widely-used sampling-based planners by finding higher-quality trajectories in less time.</summary><hostname>arXiv</hostname><author_list><author name="Tobia Marcucci" /><author name="Mark Petersen" /><author name="David Von Wrangel" /><author name="Russ Tedrake" /></author_list><url>https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.04422</url><publish_time>2022年5月9日0时0分</publish_time><arxiv_url>https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.04422</arxiv_url><arxiv_id>2205.04422</arxiv_id></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:2"><title>Game-Theoretic Autonomous Driving: A Graphs of Convex Sets Approach</title><summary>Multi-vehicle autonomous driving couples strategic interaction with hybrid (discrete-continuous) maneuver planning under shared safety constraints. We introduce IBR-GCS, an Iterative Best Response (IBR) planning approach based on the Graphs of Convex Sets (GCS) framework that models highway driving as a generalized noncooperative game.
