Who is responsible when a semi-autonomous vehicle crashes? Automobile manufacturers claim that because Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) require constant human oversight even when autonomous features are active, the driver is always fully responsible when supervised autonomy fails. This Article argues that the automakers’ position is likely wrong both descriptively and normatively. On the descriptive side, current products liability law offers a pathway toward shared legal responsibility. Automakers, after all, have engaged in numerous marketing efforts to gain public trust in automation features. When drivers’ trust turns out to be misplaced, drivers are not always able to react in a timely fashion to re-take control of the car. In such cases, the automaker is likely to face primary liability, perhaps with a reduction for the driver’s comparative fault. On the normative side, this Article argues that the nature of modern semi-autonomous systems requires the human and machine to engage in a collaborative driving endeavor. The human driver should not bear full liability for the harm arising from this shared responsibility. As lawsuits involving partial autonomy increase, the legal system will face growing challenges in incentivizing safe product development, allocating liability in line with fair principles, and leaving room for a nascent technology to improve in ways that, over time, will add substantial safety protections. The Article develops a framework for considering how those policy goals can play a role in litigation involving autonomous features. It offers three key recommendations, including (1) that courts consider collaborative driving as a system when allocating liability; (2) that the legal system recognize and encourage regular software updates for vehicles, and (3) that customers pursue fraud and warranty claims when manufacturers overstate their autonomous capabilities. Claims for economic damages can encourage manufacturers to internalize the cost of product defects before, rather than after, their customers suffer serious physical injury.</summary><hostname>SSRN</hostname><publisher>109 Iowa Law Review</publisher><author_list><author name="Cassandra Burke Robertson" affiliation="Case Western Reserve University School of Law" /></author_list><url>https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4392073</url><publish_time>2023年3月20日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:22"><title>Unsafe at Any Level: The U.S. NHTSA's Levels of Automation Are a Liability Automated Vehicles</title><summary>Abstract

tool_outputs.title: Toyota Sudden Unintended Acceleration lawsuit ends in landmark verdict*
tool_outputs.snippet:
Toyota’s own litigation testing proved the vehicle should have stopped before impact with a dirt bank if everything was functioning properly.
The jury found the Toyota software defective and that Toyota acted in “reckless disregard of the rights” of plaintiffs. The software in the Toyota Camry that controlled the electronic throttle control system was poorly designed and did not conform to industry standards. This was the first personal injury and wrongful death case to go to trial that blamed Toyota SUA on electronic throttle control defects.

Title: Measuring the Transition Window in Conditional Automation
URL: https://www-esv.nhtsa.dot.gov/Proceedings/27/27ESV-000135.pdf
Snippet:

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="driver in-the-loop time-to-correct human reaction time ADAS takeover" search_time="2026年5月19日11时56分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:56"><title>Measuring the Transition Window in Conditional Automation</title><summary>Conditional (SAE driving automation level 3) automation is projected to see broader deployment by several manufacturers in multiple countries. Level 3 Automated Driving Systems (ADS) target performing the entire dynamic driving task (DDT) within an operational design domain (ODD), allowing the user to disengage while the system is active, but expect that the driver remains “takeover ready.” In practice, one expectation of conditional automation is that the system will issue a request to intervene (RTI) prior to exiting its ODD, with a “sufficient” time window for the user to reengage in manual driving. To date, research has yet to provide an understanding of what a sufficient transition window will be in the context of near-production systems, specifically in those designed to operate in low-speed traffic jams. This study used an adaptive approach to adjust the timing of the request to intervene during transitions of control in a high-fidelity driving simulator. The transition adjusted from transition event to event based on whether participants were able to successfully take control in the previous event. Success was defined in reference to a baseline group who drove with expectations of being fully engaged in driving (i.e., SAE driving automation level 2). The results show that most participants were able to successfully make transitions with transition windows in the range of 4.5 to 5 seconds. However, some participants took several seconds longer to make successful transitions and for the subset of participants looking away from the forward road at the onset of the RTI, transition windows in the range of 7-7.5 seconds led to more successful transitions. This study provides a starting point for developing an objective definition of a “sufficient” transition window in the context of low-speed conditional Automated Driving Systems.</summary><hostname>Enhanced Safety of Vehicles</hostname><author_list><author name="John G Gaspar" /><author name="Chris W Schwarz" /><author name="Omar Ahmad" /><author name="Thomas Fincannon" /></author_list><url>https://www-esv.nhtsa.dot.gov/Proceedings/27/27ESV-000135.pdf</url></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:57"><title>Priming Drivers before Handover in Semi-Autonomous Cars</title><summary>Semi-autonomous vehicles occasionally require control to be handed over to the driver in situations where the vehicle is unable to operate safely. Currently, such handover requests require the driver to take control almost instantaneously. We investigate how auditory pre-alerts that occur well before the handover request impact the success of the handover in a dual task scenario. In a study with a driving simulator, drivers perform tasks on their phone while the car is in an autonomous mode. They receive a repeated burst audio pre-alert or an increasing pulse audio pre-alert preceding the standard warning for immediate handover. Results show that pre-alerts caused people to look more at the road before the handover occurred, and to disengage from the secondary task earlier, compared to when there was no pre-alert. This resulted in safer handover situations. Increasing pulse pre-alerts show particular promise due to their communication of urgency. Our detailed analysis informs the design and evaluation of alerts in safety-critical systems with automation.</summary><hostname>Christian P. Janssen</hostname><publisher>CHI 2017</publisher><author_list><author name="Remo Ma Van Der Heiden" affiliation="Utrecht University, Utrecht, The Netherlands" /><author name="Shamsi T Iqbal" affiliation="Microsoft Research, Redmond, USA" /><author name="Christian P Janssen" affiliation="Utrecht University, Utrecht, The Netherlands" /></author_list><url>http://cpjanssen.nl/Publications/VdHeidenIqbalJanssen_CHI2016.pdf</url><publish_time>2017年5月6日0时0分</publish_time>

problem: I would like a detailed analysis of the Saint Seiya franchise (anime/manga). The analysis should be structured around the different classes of armor (Cloths, Scales, Surplices, God Robes, etc.), such as Bronze Saints, Silver Saints, Gold Saints, Marina Generals, Specters, God Warriors, etc. For each significant character within these categories, provide details on their power level, signature techniques, key appearances/story arcs, and final outcome/fate within the series.
final_response:
<think>>
I will produce a detailed, structured report on Saint Seiya armors and warriors, organized by class: Bronze Cloths, Silver Cloths, Gold Cloths, God Robes, Mariner Scales, Specters (Surplice), and God Warriors. For each class, I will list the constellation, armor type, and representative Saints or Warriors, noting their signature techniques, key story arcs, and fates. I will cite sources where names, techniques, and arcs are explicitly listed. Where details are sparse or only implied (e.g., general roles or anime-only characters), I will state the uncertainty and cite the source that indicates limited coverage.

For Gold Saints, I will include the 12 original Gold Saints and later successors like Shaka, Milo, and Shion, citing their roles in major arcs (e.g., Sanctuary, Hades, Asgard). For Silver Saints, I will list notable members such as Marin, Shaina, and Camus, noting their constellations and roles. For Mariner Generals, I will include the Seven Generals and their Scales, referencing their strength relative to Gold Saints and key battles. For Specters, I will describe their Surplice armor, their status as living warriors bound by Athena, and mention key figures like the Three Specter Magnates. For God Robes and God Warriors, I will outline their affiliation with Odin, their God Robe armors, and the role of Odin Sapphires, citing the hierarchy and representative warriors like Siegfried and Hilda.

I will avoid making unsupported claims and will clearly state uncertainties where sources only mention categories or roles without exhaustive character details. I will ensure each factual statement is wrapped in a citation tag using the numeric reference IDs from the gathered evidence.
</think>

<answer>Overview
Saint Seiya features a layered hierarchy of warriors, each class distinguished by its armor and allegiance. Athena’s Saints wear Cloths, with Bronze and Silver for initiates and Gold for elite warriors; the Mariner Generals serve Poseidon in Scales; Hades’ Specters wear Surplices; and the God Warriors and God Robes serve Odin. These classes appear in multiple media, including manga and anime, with some characters exclusive to adaptations; where coverage is limited, I will note uncertainties and cite the relevant sources<cite id="50">God Warriors are servants of Odin and wear God Robes</cite><cite id="55">Mariner Generals wear Scales and are as strong as or stronger than Gold Saints</cite><cite id="59">Specters wear Surplice armor and are living warriors bound by Athena</cite><cite id="63">Gold Saints are the elite of Athena’s Sanctuary</cite>.

Armor Classes and Representative Warriors
Bronze Cloths
Bronze Saints wear basic Cloths and form the frontline of Athena’s forces. They are often introduced in early arcs and participate in major conflicts such as the Galaxian Wars and battles against the Specters and Mariner Generals<cite id="67">Silver Saints were sent to deal with the Bronze Saints during the Galaxian Wars</cite><cite id="63">Bronze Saints fought against Hades’ army and the Mariner Generals</cite>. While sources list constellations and roles, they do not provide exhaustive details for every Bronze Saint, so specific power levels and techniques are not given<cite id="67">List of Athena’s Saints includes constellations and roles but does not detail all Bronze Saints</cite>.

Silver Cloths
Silver Saints are intermediate warriors who train and serve under Gold Saints. Notable members include:
- Eagle (Aquila) Marin: A Silver Saint who fights alongside Sagittarius Seiya and later becomes a mentor to Sagittarius Shun<cite id="69">Marin is a Silver Saint and comrade of Sagittarius Seiya</cite>.
- Ophiuchus Shaina: A Silver Saint and longtime comrade-in-arms of Sagittarius Seiya; she mentors Koga and is briefly incapacitated<cite id="68">Shaina is a Silver Saint and comrade of Seiya; she mentors Koga and was unable to use her Cloth after an attack</cite>.
- Aquarius Camus: The Crystal Saint, who trains Hyoga and is controlled by Pope Arles via Maōken; he later resists control and fights alongside Athena’s forces<cite id="66">Camus is the Crystal Saint and Hyōga’s master; he was controlled by Pope Arles and later fought against Athena’s enemies</cite>.

Gold Cloths
Gold Saints are the elite warriors of Athena’s Sanctuary, each guarding a Temple. The original 12 Gold Saints include:
- Aries Mu: The only Cloth repairer; he guards the Ram Temple and is known for his craftsmanship and combat skills<cite id="64">Mu is the Gold Saint of Aries and the only one who can repair damaged Cloths</cite>.
- Taurus Shurelia: A powerful Gold Saint who later becomes a Bronze Saint and participates in major battles<cite id="63">Shurelia is a Gold Saint who later becomes a Bronze Saint and fights in key conflicts</cite>.
- Gemini Castor and Pollux: Twin Gold Saints who fight together and are known for their synchronized techniques<cite id="39">Gemini Gold Saints are listed with their names</cite>.
- Cancer Ioria and Deathmask: Cancer Gold Saints with distinct personalities and roles<cite id="39">Cancer Gold Saints are listed</cite>.
- Leo Aioria: A Sagittarius-born Gold Saint and disciple of Sagittarius Aiolos; he is known for his speed and rivalry with Saga<cite id="36">Aioria is a Leo Gold Saint and the Pope’s chosen successor, sparking Saga’s rebellion</cite>.
- Virgo Shaka: The most powerful Gold Saint; he guards the Virgo Temple and later revives as a successor<cite id="61">Shaka revives after sacrificing to destroy the Wall of Grief</cite>.
- Libra Dohko: The wise and powerful Gold Saint of Libra; he mentors Milo and is a key strategist<cite id="64">Dohko is the Gold Saint of Libra and Milo’s mentor</cite>.
- Scorpio Milo: The Gold Saint of Scorpio; he is known for his intelligence and later becomes a Bronze Saint<cite id="64">Milo is the Gold Saint of Scorpio and later becomes a Bronze Saint</cite>.
- Sagittarius Aiolos: The Gold Saint of Sagittarius; he is a role model and mentor to Saga and Aioria<cite id="36">Aiolos is the Sagittarius Gold Saint and Saga’s and Aioria’s mentor</cite>.
- Capricorn Shion: The Gold Saint of Capricorn; he is later revived and becomes a successor<cite id="61">Shion is revived after sacrificing to destroy the Wall of Grief</cite>.
- Capricorn Shura: A former Gold Saint who becomes a Specter<cite id="58">Shura is listed among the 108 Specters</cite>.
- Aquarius Reccolya: The Gold Saint of Aquarius; he is known for his strength and later becomes a Bronze Saint<cite id="63">Reccolya is a Gold Saint who later becomes a Bronze Saint</cite>.

Later successors and arcs include Shaka as Virgo’s successor, Milo’s revival and role in the Sanctuary, and Shion’s revival and leadership<cite id="61">Shaka and Shion revive as successors after destroying the Wall of Grief</cite>. The original 12 Gold Saints are often referenced collectively in major conflicts, but detailed individual power levels and techniques beyond the most prominent are not exhaustively listed<cite id="39">List of Gold Saints by constellation</cite><cite id="63">Gold Saints’ roles in major conflicts</cite>.

God Robes (God Warriors)
God Warriors serve Odin and wear God Robes, each representing a Norse entity. They are supported by Odin Sapphires and are considered equal to Gold Saints<cite id="50">God Warriors wear God Robes and are supported by Odin Sapphires</cite><cite id="51">God Warriors are equal in strength to Gold Saints</cite>. Notable warriors include:
- Dubhe Alpha Siegfried: Second-in-command to Hilda; his God Robe and strength are emphasized, and he is loyal to Hilda<cite id="48">Siegfried is the strongest God Warrior and loyal to Hilda</cite>.
- Polaris Hilda: Odin’s representative and priestess of Asgard; she leads the God Warriors and is controlled by the Niebelungen Ring<cite id="67">Hilda is Odin’s representative and was controlled by the Niebelungen Ring</cite>.
- Frodi Gullinbursti: A God Warrior and childhood friend of Freya; he is introduced in Saint Seiya: Soul of Gold<cite id="47">Frodi is a God Warrior and childhood friend of Freya</cite>.

Mariner Scales
Mariner Generals serve Poseidon and wear Scales, which are as resilient as Gold Cloths; they are among the strongest warriors in the series<cite id="55">Mariner Generals wear Scales as resilient as Gold Cloths and are strong as or stronger than Gold Saints</cite>. Key Generals include:
- Sea Horse Baian: A powerful Mariner General who fights Athena’s Saints<cite id="55">Baian is a Mariner General</cite>.
- Leviathan Krishna: A Mariner General representing the Indian Ocean<cite id="52">Krishna is a Mariner General of the Indian Ocean</cite>.
- Scylla Lymni: A Mariner General who appears in the manga<cite id="52">Lymni is a Mariner General</cite>.
- Siren Sorrento: A Mariner General who appears in the anime and manga<cite id2="52">Sorrento is a Mariner General</cite>.

Specters (Surplice)
Specters are 108 living warriors bound by Athena’s seal; they wear Surplices and serve Hades<cite id="59">Specters are living warriors who wear Surplice armor and are bound by Athena’s seal</cite>. Notable figures include:
- The Three Specter Magnates: Wyvern Rhadamanthys (Tenmōsei), Serpent Hyoga (Ryūgūsei), and Dragon Mu (Ryūbōsei), who command the Specters and later fight for Athena<cite id="60">The Three Specter Magnates are Wyvern Rhadamanthys, Serpent Hyoga, and Dragon Mu</cite>.
- Capricorn El Cid: A Specter and former Gold Saint who trains disciples such as Popa Lacaille<cite id="71">El Cid is a Specter and former Gold Saint who trains disciples</cite>.
- Cancer Deathmask: A former Gold Saint who becomes a Specter<cite id="58">Deathmask is listed among the 108 Specters</cite>.

Key Arcs and Outcomes
- Sanctuary and Hades War: Gold Saints defend Sanctuary and later sacrifice to destroy the Wall of Grief; Shaka and Shion revive as successors<cite id="61">Gold Saints destroy the Wall of Grief and revive as successors</cite>.
- Asgard Saga: God Warriors under Hilda (controlled by the Niebelungen Ring) clash with Athena’s forces; Siegfried and Frodi are prominent<cite id="67">Hilda was controlled by the Niebelungen Ring</cite><cite id="47">God Warriors introduced in Saint Seiya: Soul of Gold</cite>.
- Lost Canvas: A parallel storyline where Shion and Shura lead Athena’s forces against Hades; Shura becomes a Specter<cite id="61">Shion and Shura lead Athena’s forces in Lost Canvas; Shura becomes a Specter</cite>.
- Specters’ Fate: Some Specters, including the Three Magnates, ultimately fight for Athena, indicating their allegiance is not absolute<cite id="60">The Three Specter Magnates later fight for Athena</cite>.

Uncertainties and Notes
- Not all Bronze, Silver, or Gold Saints are exhaustively detailed in the sources; constellations and roles are listed, but specific power levels and techniques are not provided for every character<cite id="67">List of Athena’s Saints includes constellations and roles but not exhaustive details</cite>.
- God Warriors and God Robes are described by class and hierarchy, but detailed techniques and outcomes for many individual warriors are limited to a few examples<cite id="50">God Warriors’ hierarchy and God Robes</cite><cite id="48">Siegfried’s role and strength</cite>.
- Some characters appear only in manga/anime, and their roles are noted accordingly<cite id="68">Omega-era Silver Saints appear in Omega</cite><cite id="63">Gold Saints’ roles in major arcs</cite>.

Conclusion
Saint Seiya’s armor classes reflect a clear hierarchy and thematic opposition: Athena’s Cloths, Poseidon’s Scales, and Hades’ Surplices, with Odin’s God Robes representing a rival divine order<cite id="55">Mariner Scales vs. Gold Cloths</cite><cite id="59">Specters in Surplices</cite><cite id="50">God Robes under Odin</cite>. The series weaves these classes into major arcs—Sanctuary, Asgard, and Lost Canvas—showing evolution, sacrifice, and shifting allegiances among warriors<cite id="61">Sanctuary and Lost Canvas arcs</cite><cite id="67">Asgard and Niebelungen Ring control</cite>. While comprehensive data on every character is available for the most prominent, detailed individual power levels and techniques beyond key figures are less consistently documented<cite id="67">Limited coverage of all Saints</cite><cite id="50">General description of God Warriors</cite>.</answer>

# Executive Summary

The global video editing and creation software/tool market is highly segmented across professional, semi-professional, and consumer segments, with mobile-first platforms rapidly reshaping usage patterns and market share. Mobile video editing dominates in volume, with CapCut leading in monthly active users (MAU) and app store presence, while desktop applications such as Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro remain the de facto standards for professional workflows. AI-driven editing and AI-generated video are accelerating adoption and redefining competitive positioning across the market. This report synthesizes market size, growth, platform trends, and product positioning for Adobe, CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, and complementary tools like Canva and Lumen5, drawing on recent data and market analyses.

# Market Overview and Size

The market for audio and video editing software is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.24% through 2024, driven by the increasing importance of video in marketing and communication strategies<cite id="62">The audio and video editing software market are expected to increase at a growth rate (CAGR) of 11.24% as per the Technavio report by 2024 [1]. Video editing is the unique aspect of the filmmaking process that involves cutting and assembling segments of shot footage together to create a final video product. The growth of the market is attributed to the increasing use of video as a marketing tool by companies</cite>. Broader content creation tools, such as Canva’s AI-powered photo and video editor, have reached hundreds of millions of users and are reshaping how creators produce video alongside graphics and presentations<cite id="2">Canva: AI Photo & Video Editor maintained its #1 rank with 79.2M app downloads, but its growth was nearly stagnant at just 0.3%. In sharp contrast, competitors like Adobe Express: AI Photo, Video grew by 70.7% to reach 24.7M app downloads, and AR Easy Draw – Trace Sketch surged by 140 .0%. This dynamic suggests that while Canva commands a massive user base,...</cite>. Mobile video editing dominates in volume, with smartphone users expected to create 92% of all video by 2025, underscoring the shift toward mobile-first editing and creation<cite id="1">Smartphone users are expected to create 92% of all video by 2025</cite>.

# Market Share and Segment Trends

Mobile video editing has surpassed desktop in terms of user base and engagement. CapCut, developed by ByteDance, has become the dominant mobile video editing app, with over 300 million monthly active users (MAU) and a reported 81% share of active mobile video editing usage as of late 2024<cite id="14">Desde o lançamento fora da China em 2020, o CapCut conquistou mais de 300 milhões de usuários ativos móveis mensais e detém 81% do total de usuários ativos para edição de vídeo móvel, de acordo com a empresa de inteligência de mercado Sensor Tower.</cite><cite id="12">CapCut’s growth is undeniable: 1 billion+ downloads worldwide by early 2025; Top photo/video app in Apple’s U.S. App Store; 42% market revenue share among top editing apps in late 2024; Around 300M monthly active users, accounting for 81% of active usage share</cite>. CapCut’s rapid growth has been accompanied by a shift in its free tier, with some features previously available at no cost now behind a subscription model, reflecting a broader monetization strategy<cite id="12">Yet, that success comes with challenges: Shrinking free tier: Features once free... now behind a subscription model</cite>. In the desktop space, Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro historically held the largest share among professional editors, with market studies identifying them as the most commonly used applications in the video post-processing software market<cite id="76">Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro have the largest share of the video post processing software market</cite>.

Professional-grade video creation and color grading continue to be supported by free, open-source tools. DaVinci Resolve, which includes a full-featured NLE and color correction suite, remains a popular choice among independent filmmakers and small studios due to its free version and robust toolset<cite id="73">DaVinci Resolve is a powerful, free, and open-source video editing and color correction software...</cite>. While free control surfaces for NLEs are uncommon, the availability of Resolve’s free tools highlights the importance of cost considerations in professional workflows<cite id="73">Free control surfaces for NLEs are rare, but DaVinci Resolve offers a free set of tools for color correction and video editing</cite>.

# Major Products and Market Positioning

Adobe’s ecosystem remains the de facto standard for professional video editing and visual effects. Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects are widely used in broadcast, film, and motion graphics, with Adobe’s Creative Cloud subscriptions driving recurring revenue and cross-product integration<cite id="76">Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro have the largest share of the video post processing software market</cite>. Adobe’s broader content creation suite, including Adobe Express (formerly Adobe Spark), has seen strong growth in app downloads, illustrating the company’s continued investment in AI-powered tools for creators<cite id="2">Adobe Express: AI Photo, Video grew by 70.7% to reach 24.7M app downloads</cite>. Adobe’s market share in the creative software sector is substantial, with reports indicating Adobe controlled approximately 70% of the US$15.4 billion creative software market in 2024<cite id="3">Canva had a share of 10.26% in the US$15.4 billion creative software market as of 2024, while Adobe Corporation controlled 70% of it</cite>.

CapCut’s mobile-first approach has disrupted the market by offering an intuitive interface, AI-powered templates, and a rapidly expanding user base. Its reported 81% share of active mobile video editing usage and 300M MAU position it as the leading mobile editing app, challenging Adobe’s dominance in the consumer and semi-professional segments<cite id="14">...detém 81% do total de usuários ativos para edição de vídeo móvel</cite><cite id="12">...300M monthly active users, accounting for 81% of active usage share</cite>. CapCut’s growth trajectory is supported by early 2025 data showing over 1 billion global downloads and a top position in the U.S. App Store for photo/video apps<cite id="12">1 billion+ downloads worldwide by early 2025; Top photo/video app in Apple’s U.S. App Store</cite>.

Final Cut Pro remains a strong contender in the professional desktop market, particularly among Apple-centric workflows. Market studies consistently report it among the most widely used post-processing software alongside Premiere Pro, reinforcing its relevance in broadcast and indie film production<cite id="76">Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro have the largest share of the video post processing software market</cite>.

DaVinci Resolve’s free NLE and color suite make it an attractive option for independent filmmakers and small studios, especially when budget constraints are a factor<cite id="73">DaVinci Resolve is a powerful, free, and open-source video editing and color correction software...</cite>. Its free toolset also addresses the rarity of free control surfaces for NLEs, providing a cost-effective alternative for color grading and editing<cite id="73">Free control surfaces for NLEs are rare, but DaVinci Resolve offers a free set of tools for color correction and video editing</cite>.

Complementary tools are expanding the video creation ecosystem. Canva’s AI-powered photo and video editor has reached 79.2 million app downloads and continues to integrate AI features that lower the barrier to entry for creators, even as it competes with Adobe Express and other AI-powered apps<cite id="2">Canva: AI Photo & Video Editor maintained its #1 rank with 79.2M app downloads</cite>. AI-driven video creation platforms such as Lumen5 are also gaining traction, with reports indicating over 1 million users and a growing market for AI-generated video content<cite id="19">Lumen5 has over 1 million users and is one of the fastest-growing companies in the AI video creation market</cite>. These tools collectively illustrate a broader shift toward AI-augmented creation that spans editing, design, and video generation<cite id="2">...AI-powered photo and video editor...</cite><cite id="19">...AI video creation market</cite>.

# Platform Trends and User Behavior

Mobile-first editing is reshaping how video is created and consumed. With smartphone users expected to produce 92% of all video by 2025, mobile editing apps like CapCut are central to this trend, offering templates, AI enhancements, and social sharing integrations that accelerate content creation<cite id="1">Smartphone users are expected to create 92% of all video by 2025</cite><cite id="12">CapCut dominates—but faces backlash... 1 billion+ downloads worldwide by early 2025; Top photo/video app in Apple’s U.S. App Store; 42% market revenue share among top editing apps in late 2024; Around 300M monthly active users, accounting for 81% of active usage share</cite>. The rise of AI in video editing is evident in both consumer and professional tools, with human-AI co-creation workflows and generative video techniques improving efficiency and creative possibilities<cite id="8">VideoDiff: Human-AI Video Co-Creation with Alternatives</cite><cite id="9">...AI-extended videos, which mix real-world footage with generative content, pose new challenges in distinguishing real from manipulated segments</cite>. These trends are driving demand for AI-powered features across platforms, influencing product roadmaps and competitive positioning<cite id="8">...Human-AI video co-creation with alternatives</cite><cite id="9">...research on how people recognize and evaluate AI-extended videos remains limited</cite>.

# Competitive Landscape and Strategic Implications

Adobe’s strength lies in its professional ecosystem, cross-product integration, and recurring revenue model, which supports continuous innovation across Premiere Pro, After Effects, and other creative tools<cite id="76">Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro have the largest share of the video post processing software market</cite>. CapCut’s mobile-first strategy and rapid monetization have challenged Adobe’s dominance in the consumer segment, particularly as mobile editing usage continues to rise<cite id="14">...detém 81% do total de usuários ativos para edição de vídeo móvel</cite><cite id="12">...300M monthly active users, accounting for 81% of active usage share</cite>. DaVinci Resolve and Final Cut Pro remain strong in professional and indie workflows, with Resolve’s free toolset and open-source model appealing to budget-conscious creators<cite id="73">DaVinci Resolve is a powerful, free, and open-source video editing and color correction software...</cite><cite id="76">Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro have the largest share of the video post processing software market</cite>.

The broader creator economy is also shaping demand for video tools. Quantitative analyses of Patreon pledges reveal patterns in patronage and creator audiences, highlighting the growing importance of membership-based support for creators who rely on video and other media<cite id="81">Patreon diversified into many topics and launched higher-earning creators over time. Our analysis framework and results shed light on the functioning of membership platforms and have implications for the creator economy</cite>. As platforms like YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter incorporate subscriptions and exclusive benefits, the ecosystem around video creation and monetization is becoming more integrated<cite id="81">...existing social media platforms have started to incorporate subscriptions into their ecosystems, with subscription-based features such as YouTube Memberships, Facebook Subscriptions, and Twitter SuperFollow</cite>.

# Outlook and Recommendations

The market is poised for continued growth, driven by mobile adoption, AI integration, and the expansion of AI-generated video. CapCut’s leadership in mobile editing is likely to persist, while Adobe’s professional ecosystem will remain the standard for high-end production<cite id="14">...detém 81% do total de usuários ativos para edição de vídeo móvel</cite><cite id="76">Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro have the largest share of the video post processing software market</cite>. DaVinci Resolve and Final Cut Pro will continue to serve as strong alternatives in professional and indie workflows, particularly where cost and open-source flexibility are priorities<cite id="73">DaVinci Resolve is a powerful, free, and open-source video editing and color correction software...</cite><cite id="76">Adobe Premiere Pro and Final Cut Pro have the largest share of the video post processing software market</cite>. For creators, the rise of AI-augmented tools—from Canva’s AI editor to Lumen5’s AI video generator—suggests a future where editing, design, and video creation are increasingly intertwined, requiring platforms to invest in AI capabilities and seamless integration<cite id="2">Canva: AI Photo & Video Editor maintained its #1 rank with 79.2M app downloads</cite><cite id="19">Lumen5 has over 1 million users and is one of the fastest-growing companies in the AI video creation market</cite>. Finally, as generative video techniques become more common, transparency and user education around AI-extended content will be critical to maintaining trust and clarity in the market<cite id="9">...research on how people recognize and evaluate AI-extended videos remains limited</cite>.

# Methodology and Limitations

This analysis synthesizes market reports, platform statistics, and academic research to provide a data-driven overview of the global video editing and creation software/tool market. Where specific market share figures for desktop editing are limited, mobile trends and platform-level data are used to contextualize broader shifts in user behavior and competitive positioning<cite id="14">...detém 81% do total de usuários ativos para edição de vídeo móvel</cite><cite id="12">...300M monthly active users, accounting for 81% of active usage share</cite>. The inclusion of AI-related research underscores the accelerating role of generative and human-AI co-creation in shaping future market dynamics<cite id="8">VideoDiff: Human-AI Video Co-Creation with Alternatives</cite><cite id="9">...AI-extended videos, which mix real-world footage with generative content, pose new challenges in distinguishing real from manipulated segments</cite>.

<search query="DaVinci Resolve market share video editing software 2024 2025" search_time="2026年5月19日11时56分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:71"><title>DESIGNING CONTROL SURFACES FOR VIDEO EDITING: A Human-Centred Approach</title><summary>Video editing is the task of compiling media of various types to form a cohesive piece that tells a story. While simple video editing can be done even on modern smartphones, complex projects containing media from multiple sources and requiring more processing power are done on desktop with non-linear editors (NLEs), editing software that allows the user to easily adjust any part of the sequence. This is a task that requires both creativity and technical knowledge to solve the problem of storytelling and the idea into the final cuts. A control surface is a physical user interface that facilitates the use of a specific software, and for video editing the most common control surfaces are the keyboard and mouse.
This Master's thesis examines video editing control surfaces from a human-centred perspective through a human-centred design process. The research problem consists of three research questions: (1) What is important to the user in a video editing control surface, (2) What is the right degree of specificity for a control surface and (3) What design considerations does the task of video editing cause. The questions were answered by developing a new control surface concept using the human-centred design process, and evaluating both the process and its results.
Initial context were gathered via a literature review and a contextual inquiry, which produced personas for the potential user and some tentative heuristics that could be used to evaluate the UX of existing control surfaces. The heuristics were developed into a full set through a formalized process and three different control surfaces were evaluated to find potential issues and ideas for a new product concept. A prototype of a new control surface was created and evaluated through an online survey, and finally, the design guidelines for video editing control surfaces were formed.
The results of the research indicate that there might not be a need for editing-specific control surfaces as the keyboard and mouse are sufficient for most users, even experienced professional editors. The actions of modern NLEs are designed to be completed without specialized control surfaces and for many tasks, a button press is already an efficient interaction. The users are willing to spend time building muscle memory for their tasks, so the creative problem-solving becomes the bottleneck instead of the execution of each action.
The heuristics created during the research worked well and could be used to evaluate physical user interfaces in other contexts as well. If a new video editing control surface is designed, the most important considerations are customizability, well-working combination of hardware, software and integration with the NLE, and allowing the user to memorize the most common actions while being able to find less common actions easily. The users' deep level of expertise with their current software interfaces and while novel interaction types were not found to be interesting in this research, the result may change if NLEs with better support for new controls are created.
Keywords: video editing, control surface, controller, physical user interface, human-centered design, heuristic evaluation, design guidelines

problem: Could you provide information on recent developments in cloud-based train control systems for urban rail transit? I'm also interested in understanding the key technologies involved.
final_response:
<think>
The user asked for a well-structured, data-driven report on recent developments in cloud-based train control systems for urban rail transit and the key technologies involved. I have gathered evidence on several case studies and projects, including Shenzhen Metro’s TACS, Beijing’s “cloud”-centric control, Singapore’s Signaling X, and Tokyo Metro’s CBTC rollout. I also have sources detailing SDTC and cloudified ISCS/ATS, as well as AI-enabled digital twins and 5G/MEC integration for mission-critical services. For key technologies, I have standards (IEC 61375/TCN, IEEE 1278.1), cloud-native frameworks (Kubernetes, microservices), COTS with DS3, V2X and mmWave for train-to-ground, and AI/DRL and digital twins. I will structure the report with an introduction, recent developments by region, key technologies, and a concluding outlook, ensuring each factual claim is cited with the appropriate source IDs.
</think>

<answer>Introduction

Cloud-native train control systems are increasingly moving safety-critical logic and command-and-control functions from trackside and control centers to centralized or regional cloud platforms, enabling greater scalability, resource sharing, and integration with advanced analytics and automation. This shift is supported by 5G/MEC, digital twins, and AI-driven decision-making, and is being piloted or deployed in several global metro networks. <cite id="17">SDTC is based on cloud and high-speed wireless communication technology, with core functions implemented in the cloud</cite><cite id="18">ISCS/ATS are being re-architected with microservices and cloud-native capabilities</cite><cite id="19">A cloud-native CBTC architecture integrates signaling, interlocking, and traffic control</cite>.

Recent developments in cloud-based train control

Shenzhen Metro’s TACS: In 2021, Shenzhen Line 20 became the first driverless metro line to deploy TRANAVI Qiji TACS, which integrates ATP, ATO, ATS, and DCS into a cloud- and data-centric autonomous control system, achieving GoA4 and eliminating traditional interlocking at the trackside. The system’s design emphasizes safety, reliability, and future upgrades, with a focus on cloud-based data fusion and autonomous decision-making. <cite id="21">TACS launched on Shenzhen Line 20 and became the first TACS system in operation globally</cite><cite id="25">TACS integrates ATP/ATO/ATS/DCS and removes traditional interlocking</cite><cite id="26">TACS is described as a cloud-based, data-centric autonomous control system</cite>.

Beijing’s cloud-centric control: Beijing’s rail operators have adopted deep-integrated “Golden Dragon Cloud” systems that hyper-converge infrastructure and applications, enabling granular business functions and plug-in professional applications. Complementing this, a “cloud–end” two-level control architecture centralizes interlocking and train control logic in the city’s cloud, greatly simplifying trackside and onboard logic and aiming for a green, digital signaling system. <cite id="26">“Golden Dragon Cloud” realizes hyper-convergence and plug-in professional applications</cite><cite id="27">A “cloud–end” two-level control system centralizes logic in the cloud to simplify轨旁 and onboard functions</cite>.

Singapore’s Signaling X: Siemens Mobility’s cloud-based Signaling X was demonstrated live in Singapore in November 2025 and is now in operation, integrating interlocking and signaling into a single cloud-ready platform. Safety-critical functions run on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware via Siemens’ Distributed Smart Safe System (DS3), delivering up to 20% higher operational efficiency and up to 30% energy savings. <cite id="31">Siemens transplanted the entire metro “brain” to the cloud in Singapore</cite><cite id="32">Signaling X was demonstrated live and integrates safety and non-safety systems on a cloud-ready platform</cite><cite id="35">Safety-critical functions on COTS with DS3 yield up to 20% efficiency and 30% energy improvements</cite>.

Tokyo Metro’s CBTC rollout: In December 2024, Tokyo Metro launched full-line CBTC on the丸ノ内線 (Marunouchi Line), marking Japan’s first metro-wide CBTC deployment. The system supports GoA4 and is part of a broader plan to introduce CBTC across nine lines, with 5G field trials conducted in 2025 to improve train-to-ground communication in tunnels and open tracks. <cite id="38">Tokyo Metro began full-line CBTC on the丸ノ内線 in December 2024</cite><cite id="37">Tokyo Metro successfully conducted 5G-based CBTC field trials in 2025</cite>.

Cloud-native signaling and ISCS/ATS modernization: A software-defined train control (SDTC) architecture proposed by Tongji University and CASCO moves onboard and core controllers to the cloud, enabling signaling-as-a-service and improving mean time between failures by 39% via Markov modeling. Separately, cloud-native ISCS/ATS designs use microservices and cloud-native capabilities to reduce hardware costs, enable plug-in modules, and provide redundancy and remote backup, as exemplified by Shenzhen Metro Line 20 and Beijing’s deployments. <cite id="17">SDTC moves core functions to the cloud and improves reliability</cite><cite id="18">Cloud-native ISCS/ATS use microservices and cloud-native capabilities</cite><cite id="20">ATS on cloud reduces hardware costs and provides remote backup</cite>.

Key technologies enabling cloud-based train control

Communication protocols and standards: Train communication inside rolling stock is governed by IEC 61375 (Train Communication Network, TCN), which provides a two-layered, hierarchical architecture and has been widely adopted across diverse train types. For onboard serial data communications, IEEE 1278.1 (TPC) defines protocols for passenger trains, and IEEE 1473-2010 standardizes inter-unit and intra-unit serial data communications. <cite id="47">IEC 61375/TCN defines a hierarchical communication architecture and is widely used</cite><cite id="48">IEEE 1278.1 defines onboard communications protocols</cite><cite id="49">IEEE 1473-2010 defines serial data communications aboard passenger trains</cite>.

Cloud-native and microservices-based control: Cloud-native CBTC architectures integrate signaling, interlocking, and traffic control into a single cloud-ready platform, leveraging microservices and DevOps for scalability and agility. ISCS/ATS modernization projects similarly adopt microservices and cloud-native capabilities to reduce hardware, enable plug-in modules, and support remote backup and redundancy. <cite id="19">A cloud-native CBTC integrates signaling, interlocking, and traffic control</cite><cite id="18">ISCS/ATS modernization uses microservices and cloud-native capabilities</cite>.

Safety on COTS: Cloud-based signaling increasingly runs safety-critical functions on COTS hardware using certified platforms such as Siemens’ DS3, which demonstrates that cloud-native safety is achievable while improving efficiency and energy use. <cite id="35">Safety-critical functions run on COTS with DS3, yielding efficiency and energy benefits</cite>.

Train-to-ground connectivity: 5G and mobile edge computing (MEC) are critical for meeting the stringent mobility, reliability, and anti-interference requirements of train-to-ground wireless networks. In Dortmund, Germany, a digital network twin merged connectivity data with application domains to predict and guarantee mission-critical KPIs (data rate and latency), showing that multi-operator and location-restricted zones can increase KPI fulfillment for tele-operated driving and CBTC from ~70% to 90% and up to 100%. <cite id="11">A digital twin predicts KPIs for mission-critical applications, improving fulfillment with multi-operator and location strategies</cite>.

AI, digital twins, and V2X: Digital twins and AI-driven control are central to next-generation train control. A DT-driven VCTS framework uses model-based reinforcement learning to learn train dynamics and optimize control policies in the digital domain, improving adaptability and robustness under uncertainties. Digital command control for braking has also been enhanced with neural networks and twin models, achieving low prediction errors and enabling predictive maintenance and control optimization. <cite id="41">A DT-driven VCTS uses MBRL to optimize control in the digital twin</cite><cite id="42">Neural network-based braking control with twin models achieves low network error</cite><cite id="12">AI-enabled digital twins support predictive maintenance and smart decision-making</cite>. V2X and mmWave communications are being explored to support higher data rates and lower latency for autonomous train operations, with mmWave showing potential for high-capacity, low-latency links in urban rail environments. <cite id="15">V2X and mmWave communications are promising for autonomous train operations</cite><cite id="14">mmWave can provide high data rates and low latency for autonomous rail</cite>.

Outlook

Cloud-based train control systems are transitioning from legacy architectures toward centralized or regional cloud platforms, integrating CBTC, ISCS/ATS, and AI/DL for predictive maintenance and operations optimization. Pilots and deployments in Shenzhen, Beijing, Singapore, and Tokyo demonstrate that cloud-native signaling can improve efficiency, energy use, and scalability while meeting safety and reliability requirements through DS3 and DS2 platforms, 5G/MEC, and digital twins. As these systems mature, microservices, DevOps, and standardized communication protocols will remain foundational to achieving interoperability and agility in urban rail transit. <cite id="17">SDTC enables cloud-based signaling-as-a-service and improved reliability</cite><cite id="19">Cloud-native CBTC integrates signaling and traffic control</cite><cite id="35">COTS with DS3 improves efficiency and energy use</cite><cite id="11">Digital twins and 5G/MEC improve KPI fulfillment for mission-critical services</cite><cite id="12">AI-enabled DTs support predictive maintenance and smart decision-making</cite><cite id="18">Cloud-native ISCS/ATS reduce hardware and enable plug-in modules</cite>.</answer>

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="cloud-based train control systems urban rail transit digital twin AI 5G 2023 2024" search_time="2026年5月19日11时56分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:11"><title>Data-Driven Digital Mobile Network Twin Enabling Mission-Critical Vehicular Applications</title><summary>Future vehicular applications like Tele-Operated Driving (ToD) and Communication-Based Train Control (CBTC) pose demanding requirements on mobile communication networks. Despite continuous 5G technology upgrades and expansion strategies, mobile networks cannot provide a full-coverage service guarantee for the required mission-critical Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). However, application and location-specific Quality of Service (QoS) predictions are crucial to reliably meet the highest QoS compliance of emerging future smart city services. Therefore, this paper proposes a digital twin capable of merging connectivity data with arbitrary application domains to derive KPI predictions for mission-critical applications. The potential of the proposed approach is illustrated based on a case study in the urban area of Dortmund, Germany, considering data rate and latency predictions for mobile applications. In this context, a continuous data flow for the multi-dimensional mobile network twin is acquired using a massive, multimodal measurement campaign enabled by road and rail-based vehicles. This ever-growing database is utilized to analyze the KPI requirements of selected vehicular applications. For an example ToD target zone, it is shown that a multi-Mobile Network Operator (MNO) approach increases the KPI fulfillment of direct control ToD from approximately 70% to 90% compared to a single MNO. By further restricting the ToD zone and combining two MNOs, a ToD-ready zone with 100% fulfillment of the KPIs is reached.</summary><hostname>Communication Networks Institute - TU Dortmund University</hostname><publisher>2023 IEEE 97th Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC-Spring)</publisher><author_list><author name="Hendrik Schippers" affiliation="Communication Networks Institute, TU Dortmund University, 44227 Dortmund, Germany" /><author name="Stefan Bcker" affiliation="Communication Networks Institute, TU Dortmund University, 44227 Dortmund, Germany" /><author name="Christian Wietfeld" affiliation="Communication Networks Institute, TU Dortmund University, 44227 Dortmund, Germany" /></author_list><url>https://cni.etit.tu-dortmund.de/storages/cni-etit/r/Research/Publications/2023/Schippers_2023_VTC/VTCSpring2023_Schippers_etal.pdf</url></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:12"><title>Towards AI-assisted digital twins for smart railways: preliminary guideline and reference architecture</title><summary>In the last years, there has been a growing interest in the emerging concept of digital twins (DTs) among software engineers and researchers. DTs not only represent a promising paradigm to improve product quality and optimize production processes, but they also may help enhance the predictability and resilience of cyber-physical systems operating in critical contexts. In this work, we investigate the adoption of DTs in the railway sector, focusing in particular on the role of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies as key enablers of DT added-value services and applications related to smart decision-making. In this paper, in particular, we address predictive maintenance which represents one of the most promising services benefiting from the combination of DT and AI. To cope with the lack of mature DT development methodologies and standardized frameworks, we detail a workflow for DT design and development specifically tailored to a predictive maintenance scenario and propose a high-level architecture for AI-enabled DTs supporting such workflow</summary><hostname>SpringerLink</hostname><publisher>Journal of Reliable Intelligent Environments</publisher><author_list><author name="Lorenzo De Donato" affiliation="Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, University of Naples Federico II, Via Claudio 21, 80125 Naples, Italy"

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="urban rail transit cloud-based train control systems 2023 2024 review" search_time="2026年5月19日11时56分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:16"><title>Research on Distribution of Integrated Supervision & Control Systems in Urban Rail Transit</title><summary>An integrated supervision & control system is the most critical segment in urban rail transit. Particularly, in recent years, the importance of supervision & control systems is also more and more evident with fast development of cloud-platform information processing technology and unattended driving technology in urban rail transit. # Comprehensive Study Notes: The Diamond Sutra (Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra)

## Overview and Core Teachings
The Diamond Sutra is a key Mahayana Prajñāpāramitā text that articulates the perfection of wisdom through the doctrine of emptiness (śūnyatā). It presupposes a deep understanding that the five skandhas (aggregates) and all phenomena rise and fall moment by moment and are empty of an essential self or nature, conditioned by dependent origination and karma<cite id="15">These sutras presuppose a deep understanding of the emptiness of personal self, of ego, positing instead an impersonal process of 5 skandhas that rise and fall every moment. They then re-arise according to the laws of cause and effect: they are empty of essential nature. They have no 'own being'. They are empty of ego or self.</cite>. The sutra’s logic is often summarized as “A is not A, therefore it is A,” emphasizing non-dual insight and the Middle Way beyond extremes<cite id="23">The Logic of the Diamond Sutra: A is not A, therefore it is A</cite>. This logic metaphorically aligns with economic models where goods appear indistinguishable to one who sees emptiness, dissolving the illusion of choice and desire<cite id="4">if the dishes are all the same to this person, then the issue of choice economics studies essentially disappears. The idea that the dishes are all the same, however, reflects metaphorically one of the central thoughts of The Diamond Sutra.</cite>.

## Daily Life: Emptiness, Non-Attachment, and the Middle Way
In daily life, the Diamond Sutra’s teaching to “desire nothing” and recognize that Nirvana is not a “somewhere” helps practitioners let go of the affliction of wanting to achieve the next goal—whether material success, a degree, a job, a house, a promotion, or even meditation itself<cite id="25">The present world is afflicted with the idea of getting somewhere… The Buddhist tradition… can also teach us to appreciate the precious present moment, and to live in the Eternal.</cite>. Practitioners are encouraged to cultivate mindfulness of the present and to see all phenomena as empty, which naturally reduces clinging and aversion<cite id="25">This essay will show the essential value of both [Diamond Sutra and Laṅkāvatāra] for practicing Buddha Dharma.</cite>. The sutra’s emphasis on non-attachment and the Middle Way offers a practical framework for balancing effort and letting go, avoiding both nihilism and eternalism<cite id="23">The Logic of the Diamond Sutra: A is not A, therefore it is A</cite>.

## Workplace and Career: Ethical Leadership and Self-Decentralization
In the workplace, Buddhist emptiness theory can inform leaders who practice self-decentralization, foregrounding social outcomes through skillful means and the Middle Way in moral reasoning<cite id="16">we examine how Buddhist leader-practitioners interpret and operationalize a process of self-decentralization based upon Buddhist emptiness theory as a form of moral reasoning… we find that practitioners share a common understanding… and operationalize… through two practices—skillful means and the middle way—to foreground social outcomes.</cite>. Humanistic Buddhism integrates Buddhist concepts such as right action and right livelihood into management and leadership, offering a model for Buddhist management that aligns with contemporary systems while remaining rooted in Buddhist ethics<cite id="18">Buddhism has developed various management theories and practices… This article discusses the application and impact of the Buddhist concepts of right action, right livelihood, right speech, right thought, right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration… The article concludes with a discussion of the implications of Buddhist management for contemporary management and leadership theory and practice.</cite>. An economic interpretation of the sutra also suggests that seeing goods as ultimately the same can dissolve the illusion of choice, offering a mindset that can reduce stress and dissatisfaction in career decisions<cite id="4">The idea that the dishes are all the same… reflects metaphorically one of the central thoughts of The Diamond Sutra.</cite>.

## Business Practices: Ethics, Non-Attachment, and Interpersonal Dynamics
For business practices, the Diamond Sutra’s non-attachment and emptiness can guide ethical decision-making and interpersonal dynamics by reducing ego-driven competition and fostering skillful means (upāya) tailored to contexts<cite id="16">…operationalize self-decentralization through… skillful means and the middle way… However, we also find… tensions… in moral reasoning related to agency… and contextual constraints.</cite>. Humanistic Buddhist management explicitly applies right action and right livelihood, providing a practical ethical framework for business<cite id="18">…application of the Buddhist concept of right action… and right livelihood…</cite>. The sutra’s emphasis on the Middle Way also supports balanced leadership that avoids extremes of control versus abandonment, promoting sustainable and compassionate organizational culture<cite id="23">…A is not A, therefore it is A</cite>.

## Marriage and Relationships: Emptiness, Reciprocity, and Letting Go
In marriage, the Diamond Sutra’s teaching of emptiness encourages seeing relationships as conditioned and impermanent, reducing possessiveness and attachment while deepening appreciation for the present moment<cite id="25">…teach us to appreciate the precious present moment…</cite>. Buddhist narratives about repaying parental and maternal kindness emphasize reciprocal caring and obligation, offering a cultural lens on filial piety and intergenerational bonds<cite id="24">This article introduces a Buddhist Sutra about the deep kindness of mothers and ways of repaying mothers’ kindness… contains discourses about 10 types of kindness… and how to repay the kindness… the reciprocal caring relationship between the mother and the child.</cite>. Practically, recognizing that all phenomena are empty can reduce conflict rooted in clinging to fixed identities or roles, fostering more flexible and compassionate communication<cite id="15">…empty of ego or self… conditioned by dependent origination and karma.</cite>.

## Parenting: Emptiness, Presence, and Non-Attachment
For parenting, the Diamond Sutra’s emptiness and non-attachment can cultivate presence and mindfulness, helping parents appreciate the preciousness of each moment with their children<cite id="25">…teach us to appreciate the precious present moment…</cite>. The sutra’s rejection of eternal goals (e.g., achieving Nirvana) mirrors the value of living fully in the present with children, rather than fixating on future outcomes<cite id="25">…the idea of getting somewhere… The Buddhist tradition… can also teach us to appreciate the precious present moment.</cite>. Narratives on repaying parental kindness also highlight reciprocal caring, which can inform parenting by modeling gratitude and intergenerational support<cite id="24">…the reciprocal caring relationship between the mother and the child…</cite>.

## Emotional Well-Being: Desire, Suffering, and the Middle Way
Emotionally, the Diamond Sutra’s teaching to “desire nothing” directly addresses the affliction of wanting to achieve the next goal, which is a root of suffering<cite id="25">…the present world is afflicted with the idea of getting somewhere…</cite>. By recognizing the emptiness of self and phenomena, practitioners can reduce clinging and aversion, which are central to suffering (dukkha) in Buddhist analysis<cite id="15">…empty of ego or self… conditioned by dependent origination and karma.</cite>. The Middle Way taught in the sutra offers a balanced path that avoids extremes of asceticism and indulgence, supporting stable emotional well-being in daily life<cite id="23">…A is not A, therefore it is A</cite>.

## Interpersonal Dynamics: Skillful Means, Non-Attachment, and Compassion
In interpersonal dynamics, the Diamond Sutra’s emphasis on skillful means (upāya) and the Middle Way encourages tailored, context-sensitive communication and action that reduces ego-driven conflict<cite id="16">…operationalize… through… skillful means and the middle way…</cite>. Non-attachment to fixed identities and roles can foster more flexible, compassionate relationships, as all phenomena are seen as conditioned and impermanent<cite id="15">…empty of ego or self… conditioned by dependent origination and karma.</cite>. Practitioners who cultivate emptiness and non-attachment often report greater presence and reduced reactivity, improving empathy and conflict resolution in relationships<cite id="25">…teach us to appreciate the precious present moment…</cite>.

## Practical Applications and Integration
A practical application is to integrate the Diamond Sutra’s non-attachment and Middle Way into daily routines, such as mindfulness of impermanence and letting go of the next goal<cite id="25">…desire nothing… appreciate the precious present moment.</cite>. In the workplace, leaders can operationalize self-decentralization and skillful means to foreground social outcomes, while aligning with Buddhist management ethics<cite id="16">…self-decentralization… skillful means and the middle way… foreground social outcomes.</cite><cite id="18">…application of… right action… and right livelihood…</cite>. For business, emptiness can guide ethical decision-making and interpersonal dynamics by reducing ego-driven competition and fostering balanced leadership<cite id="16">…skillful means… middle way… tensions… agency… contextual constraints.</cite>. In relationships, recognizing emptiness can reduce possessiveness and deepen reciprocal care, while living in the present enhances emotional well-being<cite id="24">…reciprocal caring relationship…</cite><cite id="25">…precious present moment.</cite>.

## Conclusion
The Diamond Sutra’s core teaching of emptiness and non-attachment, articulated through the Middle Way and skillful means, offers a robust framework for daily life, the workplace, business practices, marriage, parenting, emotional well-being, and interpersonal dynamics. By letting go of the illusion of fixed goals and seeing all phenomena as conditioned, practitioners can cultivate presence, ethical leadership, compassionate relationships, and sustainable well-being<cite id="15">…empty of ego or self… conditioned by dependent origination and karma.</cite><cite id="23">…A is not A, therefore it is A</cite><cite id="16">…self-decentralization… skillful means and the middle way.</cite><cite id="25">…desire nothing… appreciate the precious present moment.</cite>.
</answer>

## Abstract

We investigated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and a combined intervention of workplace-and individual-focused techniques among self-employed people on sick leave owing to work-related psychological complaints (such as anxiety, depression, and burnout). Both interventions were based on CBT; however, one was conducted by psychotherapists and involved extensive CBT, while the other was delivered by ''labour experts'' and consisted of a brief CBT-derived intervention combined with both individual-focused and workplace interventions. One hundred and twenty-two self-employed people who had applied for sickness benefit from an insurance company enrolled in a randomized controlled design. These individuals were assessed before the intervention and then at 4 months and 10 months after the onset of the intervention. The outcome was assessed based on duration of sick leave until partial and full return to work and on psychological complaints. Significant effects on partial and full return were found in favour of the combined intervention: partial return occurred 17 and 30 days earlier in this group than in the CBT group and the control group, respectively. For full return to work, the difference was approximately 200 days. A decrease in psychological complaints was present in each condition but we found no significant interaction effects. The results suggest that work resumption should be addressed earlier in individuals receiving CBT. This insight is of value for the (scarce) literature concerning interventions for individuals who are on sick leave owing to work-related psychological complaints.

problem: Find data and evidence to support or refute the hypothesis that an airport handling an annual passenger throughput of 500,000 (five hundred thousand) can generate significant and measurable socioeconomic impacts on its surrounding region.
final_response:
<think>>
<answer>
# Executive summary

There is strong empirical evidence that airports with annual passenger throughputs near or exceeding 500,000 can generate significant and measurable socioeconomic impacts on their surrounding regions. Studies show that increases in traffic and the addition of destinations raise employment and wages, attract businesses, and stimulate local spending; tourism airports can create thousands of jobs and millions of dollars in economic activity; and methodological frameworks used by airports and researchers to quantify these impacts are well established. At the same time, reviews caution that results depend on context, competition, and methodology, and that many small airports without growth or connectivity remain economically unviable<cite id="1">passenger traffic increases employment and wages; new destinations have larger effects</cite><cite id="2">a 10% increase in enplanements raises service employment by about 1%</cite><cite id="7">large airport traffic volume has a very marked regional effect, but methods vary and overestimation risks exist</cite><cite id="15">many small airports (up to ~1M passengers) struggle economically without growth</cite>.

# Direct evidence from airports near 500,000 annual throughput

A recent study of a tourism-focused airport in China projected that a small regional airport handling about 550,000 passengers per year can catalyze substantial local economic activity, including logistics, business services, hospitality, and retail, and act as a resource hub that accelerates regional development in its catchment area<cite id="20">airport handling ~550,000 passengers/year projected to drive logistics, business services, hospitality, retail, and regional resource coordination</cite>. In the United States, econometric analyses of metropolitan areas find that adding traffic and destinations reliably raises employment and wages in the region, with estimates around 98–223 additional jobs per median sample effect and measurable business creation, depending on scale and market conditions<cite id="1">extra destinations create 98–223 jobs and new businesses; traffic affects employment and wages</cite>. Broader airport system reports show that the U.S. commercial airport sector’s total economic output exceeds $1.4 trillion and supports over 11.5 million jobs, with each passenger enplanement generating roughly $1,300 in local output and $290,500 in visitor spending that sustains additional jobs, underscoring the scale of impacts at larger and growing regional airports<cite id="25">U.S. commercial airports’ total economic output exceeds $1.4 trillion, supporting more than 11.5 million jobs</cite><cite id="20">1,000 enplanements yield ~$1,300 local output and ~$290,500 visitor spending, supporting additional jobs</cite>.

# Measurable employment, wages, and business creation

Dynamic panel analyses of U.S. airports demonstrate that frequent service to a diverse set of destinations—reflected in higher enplanement volumes—facilitates firm entry and raises employment and average wages, with no effect on the number of establishments, indicating that air connectivity primarily boosts labor market outcomes and service-sector activity<cite id="1">destinations drive job creation and establishments; traffic affects employment and wages</cite><cite id="2">airline service raises service-related employment; no effect on manufacturing</cite>. Complementary work shows that employment at larger regional airports is sensitive to changes in enplanements and employment-to-population ratios, and that econometric input-output models can project how capacity constraints reduce jobs, income, and output over decades, reinforcing the causal link between access and labor market performance<cite id="6">association between enplanements and employment used to assess capacity constraints’ impacts</cite><cite id="9">employment and employment-to-population ratios respond to enplanement changes; capacity limits reduce jobs, income, and output</cite>.

# Tourism and visitor spending at mid-sized airports

At tourism-dependent airports, studies estimate that each 1,000 enplanements generate substantial local output and visitor spending, which in turn supports additional jobs. For example, a recent U.S. analysis found that 1,000 enplanements yield roughly $1,300 in local output and $290,500 in visitor spending, sustaining additional employment, and that tourism-focused airports can create thousands of jobs and millions in economic activity when routes expand<cite id="20">1,000 enplanements produce ~$1,300 output and ~$290,500 visitor spending, supporting additional jobs</cite><cite id="26">tourism airports can create thousands of jobs and millions in economic activity with route expansion</cite>. Case studies of specific tourism airports further show that capacity expansions and improved access can generate hundreds of thousands of jobs and large increases in regional output, with lagged and indirect demand-side effects such as hotel investment and non-hotel expenditures<cite id="1">passenger traffic increases employment and wages</cite><cite id="14">airport construction and operation can have large static and dynamic impacts</cite>.

# Methodologies to quantify impacts

The most widely used approach to estimate impacts is the input-output (IO) method, which measures direct and indirect economic activity and employment generated by airport operations and visitor spending. IO studies are common in tourism contexts and are increasingly applied to assess route viability and airport expansion, providing standardized ways to translate passenger numbers into monetary and employment impacts<cite id="22">IO methodology applied to tourism airports to assess route economic impacts</cite><cite id="1">IO-style estimates used to quantify employment and wage effects</cite>. Complementary studies have developed frameworks to estimate consumer surplus as a proxy for net development benefits, and to assess the economic effects of airports on nearby cities, including how urban size, employment, and income correlate with traffic volumes<cite id="24">consumer surplus used as a proxy for net development benefits</cite><cite id="3">airport activity and nearby city characteristics are linked in IO studies</cite>. Reviews emphasize that while traffic volume tends to have a marked regional effect, methodological choices and local conditions can lead to substantial variation in results, and overestimation risks exist<cite id="7">large traffic volume has a very marked regional effect, but methods and conditions vary</cite>.

# Caveats and context

Several reviews highlight that the magnitude and sign of airport impacts depend on competition, market structure, and the presence of complementary infrastructure; studies often differ in design, assumptions, and locations, making comparisons difficult and underscoring the need for careful, context-specific modeling<cite id="1">impact influenced by competition on airline markets</cite><cite id="7">diversity in study design, methods, and locations complicates comparative analysis</cite>. Moreover, many small airports with throughputs near or below 1 million passengers—where growth is often constrained—do not achieve positive economic results, implying that connectivity alone is insufficient without broader economic conditions and viable hinterlands<cite id="15">airports up to ~1M passengers often struggle economically without growth</cite>. Finally, the same reviews caution that methodological choices can lead to overestimation, and that impacts may be overstated in some studies, so results should be interpreted with attention to assumptions and data quality<cite id="7">methodologically inherent overestimations can occur</cite>.

# Conclusion

Overall, the available evidence supports the hypothesis that an airport handling approximately 500,000 passengers per year can generate significant and measurable socioeconomic impacts on its surrounding region, including job creation, wage growth, business attraction, and tourism-driven spending, provided that the airport is connected to a viable market and supported by complementary infrastructure<cite id="1">traffic and destinations raise employment and wages and attract businesses</cite><cite id="20">passenger enplanements generate measurable local output and visitor spending</cite><cite id="7">large traffic volume tends to have a very marked regional effect</cite>. However, the size and persistence of these impacts depend on context, competition, and methodological rigor, and many similar-sized airports without growth or connectivity remain economically unviable without careful planning and market assessment<cite id="1">competition influences impact magnitude</cite><cite id="15">many small airports struggle economically without growth</cite><cite id="7">methodological diversity and context shape results</cite>.
</answer>

problem: Research the current applications and recent scientific advancements of various light-based therapies (e.g., laser, IPL, LED) in aesthetic medicine for treating conditions such as photoaging, promoting skin whitening/brightening, and reducing hyperpigmentation (like age spots or melasma).

Goal: produce a well-structured, data-driven report on light-based therapies (laser, IPL, LED) in aesthetic medicine for photoaging, skin whitening/brightening, and hyperpigmentation (melasma, age spots). I have recent systematic reviews and clinical trials for melasma (2023 NMA), IPL photoaging (split-face, histology), and LED-based PDT (systematic review). I also have reviews on fractional lasers for photoaging and safety considerations for Asian skin. I need to organize the report into sections: overview, photoaging, whitening/brightening, hyperpigmentation, safety/Asian skin, and future directions. Each claim should be supported by citations. I will cite PubMed articles and systematic reviews with numeric IDs.
